```ocaml
   there is no outcome to report and no reply to wait for. Both builders read the
   registered backend when the COMMAND IS BUILT, exactly as Processing.process
   and Nopal_http.send do — build them inside update.

   Four seams are now built in this shape (nopal_http, Processing, Preview,
   Retention). This note used to name the fourth consumer as the trigger for lifting
   a shared registry. The fourth arrived, the lift was evaluated against it, and
   it was DECLINED. What repeats across the four is not a near-identical block:
   the four backend records share nothing but the name — { process },
   { url; revoke }, { release } and { send } have no field, no arity and no
   result type in common — so what the four sites hold identically is a ref and
   a one-line setter read at four unrelated types, two lines whose only
   differing content is the type they stand at. The shape has DIVERGED exactly
   where a lift would have to bind it, and that is the ground. Two lesser ones:
   the eight lines across the four have no shared home (three in nopal_image,
   nopal_http in its own package), so a shared registry needs a fifth package or
   a widening of nopal_mvu's remit; and each register_backend is documented with
   prose about its own seam, which a shared one cannot carry — visible only on
   the attempt to write the fourth.

   No further count re-opens this. What would: a seam whose registration needs
   behaviour rather than storage, or a third package acquiring one of these
   seams. The cross-package split is NOT a ground on its own — it already
   existed when the count was three, so the trigger was set without weighing
   it. *)
```

`Retention` is this package's third seam in that shape, and the one that ends a
stored image's life. A stored image is bytes the platform holds under a handle and it
stays held until something releases it — no runtime, unmount or collector does
it — so an application that keeps storing pictures and never releases the ones
it has stopped using retains every one of them for the session. Releasing an
entry is NOT revoking a URL minted from it: `Preview.revoke` frees the URL and
leaves the entry registered and still able to mint again, `Retention.release` frees
the entry, and neither performs the other. An application finished with a
picture it was displaying asks for BOTH.

```ocaml
type Nopal_image.Retention.backend = {
  release : blob_id:string -> unit;   (* cannot fail: a handle this backend
                                         never issued, or one it has already
                                         released, is a no-op *)
}

Retention.default_backend  : backend
      (* in force before any platform registers one; releases nothing, because
         nothing can have been stored through a platform that never registered
         itself. Inert rather than raising — release reports no outcome, so a
         raise would abandon the caller with nothing to respond to. Public so a
         test can restore it. *)
Retention.register_backend : backend -> unit
Retention.release : blob_id:string -> 'msg Nopal_mvu.Cmd.t

(* release is a Cmd.perform and dispatches NO message: releasing cannot fail, so
   there is no outcome to report and no reply to wait for, and 'msg stays free
   because no message is ever made. It has no error type and no result — this is
   deliberate, not an omission, and a caller may release whatever it happens to
   hold without keeping a record of what it has already released.

   The backend is read when the COMMAND IS BUILT, as in the two seams above.
   Build it inside update. *)
```

### Scene Types (`nopal_scene`)

Pure scene description types used by `Element.draw` and `nopal_draw`. No platform dependencies.
`nopal_element` depends on `nopal_scene` (not `nopal_draw`), keeping the element DSL free of drawing algorithms.

```ocaml
(* Re-exports: Color, Paint, Transform, Path (segment types + builders), Scene *)
(* These are also available via Nopal_draw.Color, Nopal_draw.Scene, etc. *)
(* Graphic_name: the accessible-name decision every graphic route requires
   (see Element DSL). Re-exported as Nopal_element.Graphic_name, not by
   Nopal_draw. *)
```

### 2D Drawing (`nopal_draw`)

Higher-level drawing utilities built on `nopal_scene`. Re-exports all `nopal_scene` modules for convenience:

```ocaml
(* Colors — float 0.0-1.0 range *)
Color.rgba : r:float -> g:float -> b:float -> a:float -> Color.t
Color.rgb  : r:float -> g:float -> b:float -> Color.t
Color.hsla : h:float -> s:float -> l:float -> a:float -> Color.t
Color.of_hex : string -> (Color.t, string) result
Color.lerp : Color.t -> Color.t -> float -> Color.t
Color.categorical : Color.t array     (* 10 distinct colors *)

(* Paint fills *)
type Paint.t = Solid of Color.t
             | Linear_gradient of { x0; y0; x1; y1; stops }
             | Radial_gradient of { cx; cy; r; stops }
             | No_paint

(* Scene primitives *)
Scene.rect   : ?rx -> ?ry -> ?fill -> ?stroke -> x -> y -> w -> h -> unit -> Scene.t
Scene.circle : ?fill -> ?stroke -> cx -> cy -> r -> unit -> Scene.t
Scene.text   : ?font_size -> ?font_family -> ?font_weight -> ?fill -> ?anchor -> ?baseline -> x -> y -> string -> Scene.t
(* ?font_family is one Font.family, not a stack. A Custom name is escaped by
   Font.family_to_css_string in the canvas font shorthand, and that string is
   XML-escaped again in the SVG font-family attribute, so Custom "Inter" is
   font-family="&quot;Inter&quot;". *)
Scene.group  : ?opacity -> ?blend -> ?transforms -> Scene.t list -> Scene.t

(* Path building *)
Path.smooth_curve  : (float * float) list -> Path.segment list   (* Catmull-Rom spline *)
Path.straight_line : (float * float) list -> Path.segment list
Path.closed_area   : (float * float) list -> Path.segment list

(* Arcs. Angles are radians from the positive x axis; y grows downward, so
   increasing angles turn clockwise as seen. Every arc names its direction. *)
type Path.direction = Clockwise | Anticlockwise
(* Path.segment's arm: Arc_to of { cx; cy; r; start_angle; end_angle; direction } *)
Path.arc_to      : ?direction:Path.direction -> cx:float -> cy:float -> r:float
                   -> start_angle:float -> end_angle:float -> unit -> Path.segment
Path.arc_segment : ?direction:Path.direction -> cx:float -> cy:float -> r:float
                   -> start_angle:float -> end_angle:float -> unit -> Path.segment list
                   (* Move_to the start point, then the arc *)
Path.donut_arc   : ?direction:Path.direction -> cx:float -> cy:float -> inner_r:float
                   -> outer_r:float -> start_angle:float -> end_angle:float -> unit
                   -> Path.segment list
                   (* one closed ring segment: outer edge start -> end in direction,
                      inner edge end -> start in the opposite direction *)
(* ?direction defaults to Clockwise; the trailing () is required.
   Nopal_scene.Path.arc_to takes ~direction as a required argument and no (). *)

(* The shared sweep rules every renderer resolves an arc by *)
type Arc.resolved = Invalid | Sweep of { start : float; sweep : float }
    (* start reduced into [0, 2π); sweep signed, in [-2π, 2π] *)
Arc.resolve : Path.direction -> cx:float -> cy:float -> r:float
              -> start_angle:float -> end_angle:float -> Arc.resolved

(* Data-to-pixel mapping *)
Scale.create : domain:(float * float) -> range:(float * float) -> Scale.t
Scale.apply  : Scale.t -> float -> float
Scale.invert : Scale.t -> float -> float
```

**Arc rules.** Canvas and SVG both resolve every `Arc_to` through
`Arc.resolve`, which follows the text of the HTML canvas `arc()`
specification, so the two renderers cannot draw one arc two ways:

- The arc runs from the point at `start_angle` to the point at `end_angle` in
  its direction, whichever angle is larger. A `Clockwise` arc from `π` to `π/2`
  goes the long way round, sweeping `3π/2`. Draw a decreasing arc with
  `~direction:Anticlockwise` to go the short way.
- A span of a full turn or more in the given direction draws the full circle
  (a sweep of `2π` clockwise, `-2π` anticlockwise).
- Two angles naming the same point draw nothing (a sweep of `0.`): equal angles, and
  also a `Clockwise` arc from `2π` down to `0`. Chromium's own `arc()` draws a
  full circle for that one; nopal passes canvas angles it has already resolved,
  so no browser's reading decides it (a full turn's `stop` is nudged by one
  float step, so the platform's own subtraction also sees a full turn).
- A valid arc always brings the pen to its start point, even with a zero sweep.
  A zero radius is valid: the start point is the centre. When a subpath is
  already open the pen gets there with a line, so an arc never splits a path.
- An arc whose centre, radius or either angle is non-finite, or whose radius is
  negative, is `Invalid`: it adds nothing to the path and the pen stays where it
  was. Canvas makes no `arc()` call for it, so a negative radius never throws
  `IndexSizeError`, and SVG emits nothing for it.

A donut is `donut_arc` (or `Pie ~inner_radius`): its inner edge runs opposite
its outer edge, so the hole stays empty and shows
whatever is behind the chart, on canvas and in SVG.

### SVG Renderer (`nopal_svg`)

Pure SVG 1.1 string renderer for `nopal_scene` types. No platform deps — compiles native.

```ocaml
Nopal_svg.render : name:Graphic_name.t -> width:float -> height:float -> Scene.t list -> string
(* Renders a list of scene nodes to a complete SVG document string.
   Emits <defs> for gradients and clip paths. Output includes xmlns and viewBox.
   [name] sets the root <svg>'s accessible attributes, after viewBox:
   [Named n] gives role="img" aria-label="n" (n XML-escaped, TAB/LF/CR as char refs, other C0 dropped); [Decorative]
   gives aria-hidden="true" alone. They count only where the string is used
   inline or as a standalone file. A string loaded through Element.image is
   named at the image (alt) and rendered with Graphic_name.decorative, because
   assistive technology ignores an <img>'s internal SVG attributes.
   Scene.text content is escaped the same way. *)

(* Low-level formatting module, re-exported for unit testing *)
module Svg_fmt : sig
  type ctx
  val create_ctx          : unit -> ctx
  val color_to_css        : Color.t -> string
  val paint_to_fill_attr  : ctx -> Paint.t -> string
  val stroke_to_attrs     : ctx -> Paint.stroke -> string
  val transform_to_attr   : Transform.t -> string
  val transforms_to_attr  : Transform.t list -> string
  val path_to_d           : Path.segment list -> string
    (* Arc_to -> cubic Béziers of at most π/2 each over Arc.resolve's sweep;
       reaches the arc start with L inside an open subpath, M otherwise;
       an Invalid arc emits nothing *)
  val graphic_name_to_attrs : Graphic_name.t -> string
    (* the root <svg> accessibility attributes, each preceded by a space *)
  val blend_to_css        : Scene.blend -> string
  val line_cap_to_string  : Paint.line_cap -> string
  val line_join_to_string : Paint.line_join -> string
  val render_node         : ctx -> Buffer.t -> Scene.t -> unit
  val defs_to_string      : ctx -> string
end
```

Typical usage with charts:

```ocaml
let scene = Bar.scene ~data ~label ~value ~color ~width:400.0 ~height:250.0 () in
let svg_string = Nopal_svg.render ~name ~width:400.0 ~height:250.0 scene
(* name: a Graphic_name.t for inline use; Graphic_name.decorative when the
   string becomes an Element.image source, which carries the name instead *)
```

### Charts (`nopal_charts`)

Composable interactive charts built on `nopal_draw`:

```ocaml
(* Bar chart — ?domain_window clips data when ?x is also provided *)
Bar.view : name:Graphic_name.t -> data:'a list -> label:('a -> string) -> value:('a -> float)
  -> color:('a -> Color.t) -> ?x:('a -> float) -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?padding:Padding.t -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?format_tooltip:('a -> 'msg Element.t) -> ?on_hover:(Hover.t -> 'msg)
  -> ?on_leave:'msg -> ?hover:Hover.t -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t
  -> unit -> 'msg Element.t

(* Line chart — ?domain_window clips data with buffer=1, rescales Y *)
Line.view : name:Graphic_name.t -> series:'a Line.series list -> x:('a -> float) -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?padding:Padding.t -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?format_tooltip:((string * float) list -> 'msg Element.t)
  -> ?on_hover:(Hover.t -> 'msg) -> ?on_leave:'msg -> ?hover:Hover.t
  -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t
  -> ?on_pointer_down:(Element.pointer_event -> 'msg)
  -> ?on_pointer_up:(Element.pointer_event -> 'msg)
  -> ?on_wheel:(Element.wheel_event -> 'msg)
  -> unit -> 'msg Element.t

(* Area chart — Stacked | Overlapping modes; ?domain_window clips with buffer=1 *)
Area.view : name:Graphic_name.t -> series:'a Area.series list -> x:('a -> float) -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?mode:Area.mode -> ?padding:Padding.t -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?format_tooltip:((string * float) list -> 'msg Element.t)
  -> ?on_hover:(Hover.t -> 'msg) -> ?on_leave:'msg -> ?hover:Hover.t
  -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t -> unit -> 'msg Element.t

(* Pie/donut chart — inner_radius 0.0 = pie, >0.0 = donut *)
Pie.view : name:Graphic_name.t -> data:'a list -> value:('a -> float) -> label:('a -> string)
  -> color:('a -> Color.t) -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?inner_radius:float -> ?label_threshold:float
  -> ?format_tooltip:('a -> 'msg Element.t) -> ?on_hover:(Hover.t -> 'msg)
  -> ?on_leave:'msg -> ?hover:Hover.t -> unit -> 'msg Element.t

(* Scatter/bubble chart — ?domain_window clips data with buffer=0 *)
Scatter.view : name:Graphic_name.t -> data:'a list -> x:('a -> float) -> y:('a -> float)
  -> ?radius:('a -> float) -> color:('a -> Color.t) -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?padding:Padding.t -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?format_tooltip:('a -> 'msg Element.t) -> ?on_hover:(Hover.t -> 'msg)
  -> ?on_leave:'msg -> ?hover:Hover.t -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t
  -> unit -> 'msg Element.t

(* Sparkline — minimal inline chart *)
Sparkline.view : name:Graphic_name.t -> data:float list -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?color:Color.t -> ?stroke_width:float -> unit -> 'msg Element.t
```

Chart hover state: `Hover.t = { index: int; series: int; cursor_x: float; cursor_y: float }`

#### Axis Configuration

`Axis.config` is the record the `?x_axis` / `?y_axis` arguments above carry.
Paint and metrics live in a nested `appearance` record on it, so a caller
reaches axis colours through the same argument as `label` and `tick_count`
rather than a parallel one:

```ocaml
type Axis.appearance = {
  line_color : Color.t;         (* axis line stroke; default rgb 0.2 0.2 0.2 *)
  line_width : float;           (* width of the axis line AND of every tick
                                   mark — there is no separate tick width;
                                   default 1.0 *)
  tick_color : Color.t;         (* tick mark stroke; default rgb 0.2 0.2 0.2 *)
  tick_length : float;          (* tick length measured away from the plot
                                   area — below the line on X, left of it on
                                   Y; default 6.0. Ceiling 16.0: the offset
                                   placing the tick labels is private and
                                   fixed at 16.0, so a longer tick runs
                                   through them. Not validated. *)
  tick_label_color : Color.t;   (* per-tick value labels; default Color.black *)
  tick_label_size : float;      (* default 11.0. Ceiling 16.0: the private
                                   tick-label (16.0) and axis-label (32.0)
                                   offsets leave a fixed 16.0 gap, so on an X
                                   axis a larger size overlaps the axis
                                   label. Not validated. *)
  axis_label_color : Color.t;   (* the single caption drawn when config.label
                                   is Some; default Color.black *)
  axis_label_size : float;      (* default 12.0 *)
}

type Axis.config = {
  label : string option;        (* Some => an axis caption is drawn *)
  min : float option;           (* explicit domain override, else nice bounds *)
  max : float option;
  tick_count : int;             (* default 5 *)
  format_tick : float -> string;(* default string_of_float *)
  appearance : Axis.appearance; (* default Axis.default_appearance *)
}

Axis.default_appearance : Axis.appearance
Axis.default_config     : Axis.config
Axis.equal_appearance   : Axis.appearance -> Axis.appearance -> bool
(* Structural equality; float fields compare with Float.equal. There is no
   equal for config, because format_tick is a function. *)
```

The two label colours default to `Color.black` and not to the axis grey —
that is the colour an unfilled text node paints. Omitting `?x_axis` / `?y_axis`
entirely, or passing `Axis.default_config`, renders exactly as the charts did
before appearance was configurable.

Source compatibility is a separate matter from that behavioural one:
`Axis.config` gained a **required** field, so any downstream full-literal
construction or record pattern of `Axis.config` must add `appearance` to keep
compiling — or switch to `{ Axis.default_config with ... }`, which is the
recommended spelling and survives the next field addition.

`Bar` draws its own X axis line and X axis caption instead of calling
`Axis.render_x`, and reads both off `x_axis.appearance`, so a themed colour
applies to a bar chart's X axis too. Its per-bar category labels are not axis
chrome and are not configurable.

```ocaml
(* A themed axis. Spell out the eight-field appearance record in full — it is
   pure paint, and { Axis.default_appearance with ... } inherits colours the
   call site never states. Build config the other way, onto the defaults:
   config is the record the framework extends, so a full literal there turns
   the next added field into a compile error at your call site. Both sizes
   below stay under the 16.0 ceilings noted above. *)
let axis_appearance =
  { Axis.line_color = Color.rgb ~r:0.8 ~g:0.1 ~b:0.1;
    line_width = 3.0;
    tick_color = Color.rgb ~r:0.0 ~g:0.55 ~b:0.55;
    tick_length = 12.0;
    tick_label_color = Color.rgb ~r:0.1 ~g:0.2 ~b:0.6;
    tick_label_size = 15.0;
    axis_label_color = Color.rgb ~r:0.5 ~g:0.0 ~b:0.5;
    axis_label_size = 20.0 }

(* Bar reads x_axis.appearance for the X axis line and caption it draws
   itself, so pass both to theme the whole frame. *)
let x_axis =
  { Axis.default_config with
    label = Some "Quarter"; appearance = axis_appearance }

let y_axis =
  { Axis.default_config with
    label = Some "Revenue"; appearance = axis_appearance }

let chart = Bar.view ~name ~data ~label ~value ~color ~width:400.0 ~height:250.0
              ~x_axis ~y_axis ()
```

#### Scene Functions

Every chart module exposes a `scene` function that returns `Scene.t list` for
pure SVG export or embedding in composite scenes. Scene functions accept the
same data/layout parameters as `view` but omit interaction parameters
(`on_hover`, `on_leave`, `hover`, `format_tooltip`, event handlers).

```ocaml
Bar.scene       : data:'a list -> label:('a -> string) -> value:('a -> float)
  -> color:('a -> Color.t) -> ?x:('a -> float) -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?padding:Padding.t -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t -> unit -> Scene.t list

Line.scene      : series:'a Line.series list -> x:('a -> float) -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?padding:Padding.t -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t -> unit -> Scene.t list

Area.scene      : series:'a Area.series list -> x:('a -> float) -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?mode:Area.mode -> ?padding:Padding.t -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t -> unit -> Scene.t list

Pie.scene       : data:'a list -> value:('a -> float) -> label:('a -> string)
  -> color:('a -> Color.t) -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?inner_radius:float -> ?label_threshold:float -> unit -> Scene.t list

Scatter.scene   : data:'a list -> x:('a -> float) -> y:('a -> float)
  -> ?radius:('a -> float) -> color:('a -> Color.t) -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?padding:Padding.t -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t -> unit -> Scene.t list

Heat_map.scene  : data:'a list -> row:('a -> int) -> col:('a -> int)
  -> value:('a -> float) -> row_count:int -> col_count:int
  -> ?row_labels:string list -> ?col_labels:string list
  -> scale:Color_scale.t -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?padding:Padding.t -> unit -> Scene.t list

Sparkline.scene : data:float list -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?color:Color.t -> ?stroke_width:float -> unit -> Scene.t list

Trading.Candlestick.scene : data:'a list -> x:('a -> float)
  -> open_:('a -> float) -> high:('a -> float) -> low:('a -> float) -> close:('a -> float)
  -> width:float -> height:float -> ?padding:Padding.t
  -> ?bullish_color:Color.t -> ?bearish_color:Color.t
  -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t -> unit -> Scene.t list

Trading.Drawdown.scene : data:'a list -> x:('a -> float) -> y:('a -> float)
  -> width:float -> height:float -> ?padding:Padding.t
  -> ?fill_color:Color.t -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t -> unit -> Scene.t list
```

#### Heat Map

```ocaml
Heat_map.view : name:Graphic_name.t -> data:'a list -> row:('a -> int) -> col:('a -> int)
  -> value:('a -> float) -> row_count:int -> col_count:int
```
