#### Trading Namespace

Convenient grouping of trading-specific chart types:

```ocaml
module Trading : sig
  module Candlestick = Trading_candlestick
  module Drawdown = Trading_drawdown
end
```

**Candlestick chart** — OHLC candles with wicks:

```ocaml
Trading.Candlestick.view : name:Graphic_name.t -> data:'a list -> x:('a -> float)
  -> open_:('a -> float) -> high:('a -> float) -> low:('a -> float) -> close:('a -> float)
  -> width:float -> height:float -> ?padding:Padding.t
  -> ?bullish_color:Color.t -> ?bearish_color:Color.t
  -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?format_tooltip:(int -> float -> float -> float -> float -> 'msg Element.t)
  -> ?on_hover:(Hover.t -> 'msg) -> ?on_leave:'msg -> ?hover:Hover.t
  -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t -> unit -> 'msg Element.t
(* Bullish (close > open) and bearish candles use distinct colors.
   format_tooltip receives index and OHLC values. Clips via Viewport with buffer=0. *)
```

**Drawdown chart** — inverted area from 0% baseline downward:

```ocaml
Trading.Drawdown.view : name:Graphic_name.t -> data:'a list -> x:('a -> float) -> y:('a -> float)
  -> width:float -> height:float -> ?padding:Padding.t
  -> ?fill_color:Color.t -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?format_tooltip:(int -> float -> 'msg Element.t)
  -> ?on_hover:(Hover.t -> 'msg) -> ?on_leave:'msg -> ?hover:Hover.t
  -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t -> unit -> 'msg Element.t
(* Y values should be <= 0.0 (drawdown percentages). Y domain: [min_drawdown, 0.0].
   fill_color defaults to semi-transparent red. Clips via Viewport with buffer=1. *)
```

#### Color Scale

Maps data values to colors via interpolation:

```ocaml
Color_scale.sequential : low:Color.t -> high:Color.t -> Color_scale.t
Color_scale.diverging : low:Color.t -> mid:Color.t -> high:Color.t
  -> ?midpoint:float -> unit -> Color_scale.t
Color_scale.apply : Color_scale.t -> min:float -> max:float -> float -> Color.t
(* Values outside [min, max] are clamped. Diverging midpoint defaults to 0.0. *)
```

#### Domain Window

Visible X-axis range for pan/zoom:

```ocaml
type Domain_window.t = { x_min : float; x_max : float }

Domain_window.create : x_min:float -> x_max:float -> Domain_window.t
Domain_window.equal  : Domain_window.t -> Domain_window.t -> bool
Domain_window.width  : Domain_window.t -> float
Domain_window.pan    : Domain_window.t -> delta:float -> Domain_window.t
Domain_window.zoom   : Domain_window.t -> center:float -> factor:float -> Domain_window.t
(* zoom factor < 1.0 zooms in, > 1.0 zooms out. Center maintains relative position. *)

Domain_window.clamp  : data_min:float -> data_max:float -> Domain_window.t -> Domain_window.t
(* IMPORTANT: pan/zoom do NOT clamp. Always pipe through clamp after every
   pan/zoom to prevent the window from sliding past the data range:
     Domain_window.pan dw ~delta |> Domain_window.clamp ~data_min:0.0 ~data_max:999.0
   Without clamp, the chart will go blank when the user drags past the data. *)
```

Typical pan/zoom update pattern (drag-to-pan + wheel-to-zoom + button zoom):

```ocaml
(* In your model: domain_window : Domain_window.t; drag_start_x : float option *)
let clamp_dw dw = Domain_window.clamp ~data_min:0.0 ~data_max:999.0 dw

(* Drag to pan *)
| PointerDown x -> ({ model with drag_start_x = Some x }, Cmd.none)
| PointerMove x ->
    (match model.drag_start_x with
     | None -> (model, Cmd.none)
     | Some last_x ->
         let scale = Domain_window.width model.domain_window /. chart_w in
         let delta = -.(( x -. last_x) *. scale) in
         let dw = Domain_window.pan model.domain_window ~delta |> clamp_dw in
         ({ model with domain_window = dw; drag_start_x = Some x }, Cmd.none))
| PointerUp | PointerLeave -> ({ model with drag_start_x = None }, Cmd.none)

(* Wheel to zoom — on_wheel:(fun we -> WheelZoom we) *)
| WheelZoom we ->
    let frac = we.x /. chart_w in
    let center = dw.x_min +. (frac *. Domain_window.width dw) in
    let factor = if we.delta_y > 0.0 then 1.2 else 1.0 /. 1.2 in
    let dw' = Domain_window.zoom dw ~center ~factor |> clamp_dw in
    ({ model with domain_window = dw' }, Cmd.none)

(* Button zoom — zooms around center *)
| ZoomIn ->
    let center = (dw.x_min +. dw.x_max) /. 2.0 in
    let dw' = Domain_window.zoom dw ~center ~factor:0.5 |> clamp_dw in
    ({ model with domain_window = dw' }, Cmd.none)
```

#### Chart Pane

Multi-pane synchronized layout:

```ocaml
type 'msg Chart_pane.pane = {
  height_ratio : float;
  chart : Domain_window.t -> width:float -> height:float -> 'msg Element.t;
  y_axis : Axis.config option;
}

Chart_pane.pane : height_ratio:float -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> (Domain_window.t -> width:float -> height:float -> 'msg Element.t)
  -> 'msg Chart_pane.pane
(* NOTE: pane's y_axis is currently inert — the record stores it and nothing in
   Chart_pane reads it, so it neither draws nor themes an axis. Configure the
   axis on the chart the pane wraps instead. *)

Chart_pane.view : panes:'msg Chart_pane.pane list -> domain_window:Domain_window.t
  -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?on_pointer_down:(Element.pointer_event -> 'msg)
  -> ?on_pointer_move:(Element.pointer_event -> 'msg)
  -> ?on_pointer_up:(Element.pointer_event -> 'msg)
  -> ?on_pointer_leave:'msg
  -> ?on_wheel:(Element.wheel_event -> 'msg)
  -> unit -> 'msg Element.t
(* Panes are vertically stacked; height_ratios normalized to sum to 1.0.
   Each pane's chart function receives the shared domain_window plus the
   computed pixel width and height. Raw pointer/wheel events are forwarded
   so the caller can implement pan/zoom in their update function. *)
```

#### Viewport

Clips data to visible domain window:

```ocaml
Viewport.clip : x:('a -> float) -> data:'a list -> window:Domain_window.t
  -> buffer:int -> 'a list
Viewport.clip_sorted : x:('a -> float) -> data:'a array -> window:Domain_window.t
  -> buffer:int -> 'a array
(* buffer=1 for line/area (path continuity), buffer=0 for bar/scatter.
   clip_sorted uses binary search — O(log n) vs O(n). *)
```

#### Downsample (LTTB)

Reduces large datasets while preserving visual shape:

```ocaml
Downsample.lttb : x:('a -> float) -> y:('a -> float) -> data:'a array
  -> target:int -> 'a array
Downsample.should_downsample : data_length:int -> pixel_width:float -> bool
Downsample.target_for_width  : pixel_width:float -> int
(* Threshold: 3x pixels. Target: 2x pixels. First/last points always preserved. *)
```

#### Snap

Find nearest data point for crosshair/tooltip:

```ocaml
Snap.nearest_index : x:('a -> float) -> data:'a list -> target:float -> int option
Snap.nearest_index_sorted : x:('a -> float) -> data:'a array -> target:float -> int option
(* nearest_index_sorted uses binary search — O(log n). Returns None for empty data. *)
```

#### Hit Map

Hit regions now include `Band_region` for vertical-band snapping:

```ocaml
type Hit_map.region =
  | Rect_region of { x; y; w; h; hit }
  | Circle_region of { cx; cy; r; hit }
  | Wedge_region of { cx; cy; inner_r; outer_r; start_angle; end_angle; hit }
  | Band_region of { x; w; hit }    (* vertical band, full chart height *)
```

### HTTP (`nopal_http`)

Pure HTTP types and backend abstraction. Application code uses these types in `update`; platform backends provide the actual network implementation.

```ocaml
(* Response type — includes response headers *)
type response = { status : int; body : string; headers : (string * string) list }

(* Error types *)
type error =
  | Network_error of string
  | Timeout
  | Invalid_blob of string   (* a File part named a handle with no store entry;
                                carries the handle — nothing was sent *)
type outcome = (response, error) result

val message : error -> string   (* human-readable, for display *)

(* Multipart parts. A File part names its bytes by the opaque handle the web
   blob store issued (Nopal_blob_web.Blob_store.store) — binary never enters
   the OCaml heap, and only a _web backend can resolve one. *)
type part =
  | Field of string * string      (* Field (name, value) — plain string field *)
  | File of {
      name : string;              (* form field name *)
      blob_id : string;           (* opaque store handle; never fabricate one *)
      filename : string option;   (* None defers to the blob's own name *)
      mime : string option;       (* None defers to the blob's reported type;
                                     a value is a declaration, not validation *)
    }

(* Request body variants *)
type body =
  | String of { content : string; content_type : string option }
  | Json of string
  | Form_encoded of (string * string) list
  | Multipart of part list   (* no Content-Type is sent — the platform's Fetch
                                implementation generates the boundary *)
  | Empty

(* HTTP methods and request record *)
type meth = GET | POST | PUT | DELETE | PATCH
type request = {
  meth : meth;
  url : string;
  headers : (string * string) list;
  body : body;
  timeout : float option;
}

(* Backend abstraction — set once at startup *)
type backend = { send : request -> outcome Nopal_mvu.Task.t }
type cancellable_backend = {
  send_cancellable : request -> Nopal_mvu.Task.cancellation_token * outcome Nopal_mvu.Task.t
}

val default_backend : backend                              (* always dispatches Network_error *)
val default_cancellable_backend : cancellable_backend      (* wraps default_backend with Task.cancellable *)
val register_backend : backend -> unit                     (* call at startup before mounting *)
val register_cancellable_backend : cancellable_backend -> unit

(* HTTP commands — return Cmd.t for MVU integration *)
val send : request -> (outcome -> 'msg) -> 'msg Cmd.t       (* generic, any method *)
val get : ?headers:(string * string) list -> ?timeout:float
  -> string -> (outcome -> 'msg) -> 'msg Cmd.t
val post : ?headers:(string * string) list -> ?timeout:float
  -> body:body -> string -> (outcome -> 'msg) -> 'msg Cmd.t
val put : ?headers:(string * string) list -> ?timeout:float
  -> body:body -> string -> (outcome -> 'msg) -> 'msg Cmd.t
val delete_ : ?body:body -> ?headers:(string * string) list -> ?timeout:float
  -> string -> (outcome -> 'msg) -> 'msg Cmd.t
val patch : ?headers:(string * string) list -> ?timeout:float
  -> body:body -> string -> (outcome -> 'msg) -> 'msg Cmd.t

(* Cancellable variants — return token + Cmd.t *)
val send_cancellable : request -> (outcome -> 'msg)
  -> Nopal_mvu.Task.cancellation_token * 'msg Cmd.t
val get_cancellable : ?headers:(string * string) list -> ?timeout:float
  -> string -> (outcome -> 'msg) -> Nopal_mvu.Task.cancellation_token * 'msg Cmd.t
val post_cancellable : ?headers:(string * string) list -> ?timeout:float
  -> body:body -> string -> (outcome -> 'msg) -> Nopal_mvu.Task.cancellation_token * 'msg Cmd.t
val put_cancellable : ?headers:(string * string) list -> ?timeout:float
  -> body:body -> string -> (outcome -> 'msg) -> Nopal_mvu.Task.cancellation_token * 'msg Cmd.t
val delete_cancellable : ?body:body -> ?headers:(string * string) list -> ?timeout:float
  -> string -> (outcome -> 'msg) -> Nopal_mvu.Task.cancellation_token * 'msg Cmd.t
val patch_cancellable : ?headers:(string * string) list -> ?timeout:float
  -> body:body -> string -> (outcome -> 'msg) -> Nopal_mvu.Task.cancellation_token * 'msg Cmd.t
```

Usage pattern in `main.ml`:

```ocaml
(* Register the web backend before mounting *)
let () =
  Nopal_http.register_backend { Nopal_http.send = Nopal_http_web.send };
  Nopal_http.register_cancellable_backend
    { Nopal_http.send_cancellable = Nopal_http_web.send_cancellable };
  Nopal_web.mount (module My_app) target
```

Usage in `update`:

```ocaml
type msg = FetchData | GotData of Nopal_http.outcome
         | Posted of Nopal_http.outcome | Uploaded of Nopal_http.outcome

let update model = function
  | FetchData ->
      (model, Nopal_http.get "https://api.example.com/data" (fun r -> GotData r))
  | GotData (Ok { status = 200; body; _ }) ->
      ({ model with data = parse body }, Cmd.none)
  | GotData (Ok { status; _ }) ->
      ({ model with error = Some (Printf.sprintf "HTTP %d" status) }, Cmd.none)
  (* Name every constructor and render through `message`. Never collapse to
     `| GotData (Error e) ->`: that compiles forever and would silently swallow
     a future error variant. Spelling them out in one arm keeps the compiler as
     the guard while giving the app a single wording for failures. *)
  | GotData (Error ((Network_error _ | Timeout | Invalid_blob _) as e)) ->
      ({ model with error = Some (Nopal_http.message e) }, Cmd.none)
  | Posted _ -> (* handle POST response *) (model, Cmd.none)

(* POST with JSON body *)
let submit_data model =
  let body = Nopal_http.Json (encode model.form) in
  (model, Nopal_http.post ~body "https://api.example.com/data" (fun r -> Posted r))

(* POST a picked file plus a string field as one multipart/form-data request.
   [file] is the Element.file_info the file_input's on_change handed over. *)
let upload model (file : Element.file_info) =
  let body =
    Nopal_http.Multipart
      [ Nopal_http.Field ("caption", model.caption);
        Nopal_http.File
          { name = "receipt";
            blob_id = file.blob_id;
            filename = Some file.name;   (* None defers to the blob's name *)
            mime = Some file.mime }      (* None defers to the blob's type *)
      ]
  in
  (model, Nopal_http.post ~body "/api/receipt-upload" (fun r -> Uploaded r))

(* A handle with no store entry (released, or fabricated) fails the whole
   request with Error (Invalid_blob handle) before any fetch is issued — a
   partial body is never sent. *)
```

### HTTP Web Backend (`nopal_http_web`)

Browser Fetch API implementation. Returns `Task.t` values — used in `main.ml` to register the backend via `{ send = Nopal_http_web.send }`. Supports all HTTP methods, headers, request bodies, and timeouts.

```ocaml
val send : Nopal_http.request -> Nopal_http.outcome Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val get : ?headers:(string * string) list -> ?timeout:float
  -> string -> Nopal_http.outcome Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val post : ?headers:(string * string) list -> ?timeout:float
  -> body:Nopal_http.body -> string -> Nopal_http.outcome Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val put : ?headers:(string * string) list -> ?timeout:float
  -> body:Nopal_http.body -> string -> Nopal_http.outcome Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val delete_ : ?body:Nopal_http.body -> ?headers:(string * string) list -> ?timeout:float
  -> string -> Nopal_http.outcome Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val patch : ?headers:(string * string) list -> ?timeout:float
  -> body:Nopal_http.body -> string -> Nopal_http.outcome Nopal_mvu.Task.t

val send_cancellable : Nopal_http.request
  -> Nopal_mvu.Task.cancellation_token * Nopal_http.outcome Nopal_mvu.Task.t

(* All functions use the browser Fetch API. Network failures produce
   Error (Network_error msg), timeouts produce Error Timeout — never
   a raised exception. send_cancellable aborts via AbortController on cancel.

   A Multipart body resolves each File part's blob_id against
   Nopal_blob_web.Blob_store and appends the stored Brr.Blob.t itself, so the
   bytes are never read into OCaml. An unresolvable handle produces
   Error (Invalid_blob handle) — again never a raised exception — and fails the
   whole request: no fetch is issued, so no other part is sent either. *)
```

### Blob Store (`nopal_blob_web`)

Session-local registry mapping opaque handles to browser blobs. Binary data
stays on the JavaScript side: a handle is the only thing that crosses into a
natively-compiled package, so a `_web` backend that needs the bytes resolves the
handle here. A leaf package — it does not depend on the renderer, so an
HTTP-only bundle can resolve handles without pulling `nopal_web` in.
Re-exported as `Nopal_web.Blob_store` for applications that already depend on
the renderer.

```ocaml
val store  : Brr.Blob.t -> string        (* fresh handle; never deduplicates, never recycles *)
val lookup : string -> Brr.Blob.t option (* None for an unknown or released handle — never raises *)
val object_url : string -> string option (* a URL that DISPLAYS the handle's blob *)
val revoke_url : string -> unit          (* release one; idempotent *)
val remove : string -> unit              (* idempotent *)
val clear  : unit -> unit

(* Handles carry a random per-session component, so a fabricated literal cannot
   alias a live entry. The shape is not part of the interface — do not parse or
   construct one. Entries live for the page session and are released only by an
   explicit remove/clear: unmounting a Nopal application does NOT clear them, so
   an upload in flight at teardown keeps a working handle (feature 0122,
   Decision 1). Release is the application's responsibility. *)

(* object_url answers None for a handle that resolves to nothing AND for an
   environment that mints no URL for it — an absence either way, never an error
   and never an exception, matching lookup's own contract. The minted URL is
   same-origin and meaningless outside the page session that issued it, exactly
   like the handle it came from.

   The lifetime is a caller obligation, and it is the sharp edge of this module.
   A live URL PINS its blob: the bytes stay resident even after the entry behind
   them is released with remove/clear, and unmounting releases neither. Only
   revoke_url releases the URL. A view that replaces one image with another
   revokes the URL it is replacing, or every photograph the user takes is held
   for the rest of the session. Every call mints a SEPARATE URL, including
   repeated calls with the same handle, so two mints are two revokes rather than
   one — there is no memoisation, deliberately, because memoising would make the
   store own a lifetime this interface says it does not own.

   revoke_url is idempotent and a no-op on a string this store never minted, so a
   caller releasing whatever it happens to hold needs no bookkeeping to avoid a
   double release. It releases the URL only: the entry stays registered and can
   mint again. Use remove to release that.

   Application code does not call these directly — Nopal_image.Preview is the
   platform-free seam, and Nopal_image_web wraps these two functions into it. *)
```

### Image Web (`nopal_image_web`)

Browser implementation of `Nopal_image.Processing`, of `Nopal_image.Preview` and of
`Nopal_image.Retention`.
The processing half decodes a stored image,
scores its sharpness, downscales it natively on a detached canvas and
re-encodes it back into `nopal_blob_web` under a fresh handle. Returns a
`Task.t` — used in `main.ml` to register the backend via
`{ Nopal_image.Processing.process = Nopal_image_web.process }`. The encoded bytes
never enter the OCaml heap; pixels cross the js_of_ocaml boundary exactly once,
on the smaller sharpness canvas only, and only after the browser has done the
downscaling itself.

The worked example is the kitchen sink's "Receipt Capture" section
(`examples/kitchen_sink/sub_receipt_flow.ml`), which is also this package's only
real-browser coverage: `test/e2e/tests/kitchen-sink-receipt-flow.spec.ts` drives
it in headless Chromium. Read it for the shape of a consumer — the section names
its own `Config` rather than inheriting `Config.recommended`, holds the processed
`result_info` in the same model arm as the upload state so the upload cannot name
the picked handle by accident, and matches `Processing.error` exhaustively. That
same arm also carries the byte length of the file the pass consumed, taken from
the `Element.file_info` that passed the guard: the two lengths the section reports
are then provably one photograph's, where reading the picked length back off the
selection at render time would need an option the compiler cannot see is full.

It is also the reference for preview hygiene, which is easy to get subtly wrong:
the preview lifecycle is ONE variant (never a pair of `string option`s) carrying
a generation counter, a replacement emits the revocations before the new requests
in a single batch, a URL delivered for a superseded generation is released on
arrival instead of stored, and the transition into the failure arm releases the
half of the pair that had already arrived — that arm carries no URL, so nothing
else would ever release it. Entry-release hygiene sits beside it and is
independent of it: revoking a URL leaves its entry registered and able to mint
again, so neither operation performs the other, and every arm that lets go of a
photograph owes BOTH a revoke and a release. The arms owe different sets —
replacing the selection, re-shooting and clearing the picker let go of the
picked photo and the encode measured from it; a second pass answering for a
photo still picked lets go of the encode alone, whether it succeeded or failed,
since the picker still names the photo that encode was made from.

```ocaml
val process : blob_id:string -> config:Nopal_image.Config.t
  -> (Nopal_image.Processing.result_info, Nopal_image.Processing.error) result
     Nopal_mvu.Task.t

(* Stage order: blob lookup → decode → metric-canvas draw at
   Dimensions.fit ~max_edge:(Config.metric_edge config) → one pixel read →
   Sharpness.score → upload-canvas draw at
   Dimensions.fit ~max_edge:(Config.max_edge config) → encode with
   Config.format_to_mime (Config.format config) at Config.quality config →
   Blob_store.store. The score is taken FIRST, and its inputs are the decoded
   image and the metric edge, both known at the decode — so the order against
   the encode is free, and taking it first leaves no step below the store that
   can fail. The blob's byte length and the two canvas dimension reads are taken
   BEFORE Blob_store.store is asked, so nothing at all stands between the store
   and the delivery, no failure strands a stored entry nobody holds a handle to,
   and a pass that cannot be scored stores nothing. A pass that would fail BOTH
   its score and its encode reports the score, because the encoder was never
   asked.

   The decoded bitmap is released on every exit path, success
   and failure alike, and exactly once: the release and the delivery are one
   action behind a one-shot latch, because the region around the delivery
   finishes again when an application's dispatch raises.

   The task is built with Nopal_mvu.Task.guard_once, not Task.guard. The handle
   lookup delivers synchronously, inside the guard's own try; a guard holding the
   raw resolver would answer a raising dispatch with a second outcome.

   Failures are classified by WHICH STAGE raised, never by the text of the
   browser's message. Note the consequence: a browser with no createImageBitmap
   fails at the decode stage and therefore reports Decode_failed, NOT
   Canvas_unavailable. An application testing for an unsupported environment must
   treat Decode_failed as covering that case too. Canvas_unavailable means the 2D
   context was refused, or that no backend was registered at all. *)
```

The preview half wraps `nopal_blob_web`'s object URLs into `Nopal_image.Preview`,
so a section can display a stored image without importing `Brr`. Registered in
`main.ml` beside the processing backend, once, before any command is built.

```ocaml
val preview_url : blob_id:string
  -> (string, Nopal_image.Preview.error) result Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val revoke_preview_url : url:string -> unit

(* Registration:
     Nopal_image.Preview.register_backend
       { Nopal_image.Preview.url = Nopal_image_web.preview_url;
         revoke = Nopal_image_web.revoke_preview_url }

   The two ways there can be no URL are kept apart because they have different
   owners: a handle the store resolves to nothing is Blob_not_found and the
   application is holding a stale handle; a handle it DOES resolve for which the
   browser still produced no URL — no notion of an object URL at all, or a
   refused call — is Url_unavailable and the platform is the reason. The mint
   runs inside the Task rather than while the command is built, behind
   Nopal_mvu.Task.guard_once, so a browser that refuses reports a failure of the
   effect instead of raising out of the application's update.

   Lifetime as in nopal_blob_web: the minted URL pins the image until
   revoke_preview_url releases it, nothing else releases it, and every call mints
   its own — two mints are two releases. revoke_preview_url is idempotent, is a
   no-op on a string this browser never minted or in an environment with no
   object URLs at all, and releases the URL only: the store entry stays
   registered and can mint again. *)
```

The release half hands `nopal_blob_web`'s entry removal to `Nopal_image.Retention`.
Registered in `main.ml` beside the other two, once, before any command is built.

```ocaml
val release : blob_id:string -> unit

(* Registration:
     Nopal_image.Retention.register_backend
       { Nopal_image.Retention.release = Nopal_image_web.release }

   Idempotent, total, and a no-op on a handle this store never issued or has
   already released, so a caller releasing whatever it happens to hold needs no
   bookkeeping to avoid a double release. It reports no outcome at all, here as
   in the store beneath it.

   Releasing an entry is NOT revoking a URL, and neither performs the other. A
   URL already minted from an entry keeps the image's bytes resident after the
   entry is released and only revoke_preview_url frees them; releasing the entry
   leaves that URL still displaying the image. An application finished with a
   photograph it was displaying asks for BOTH. *)
```

```ocaml
Dimensions.fit : src_width:int -> src_height:int -> max_edge:int -> int * int
(* Pure long-edge sizing, no platform types. Preserves aspect to within a whole
   pixel; the longer returned edge is exactly max_edge whenever a cap applies; a
   source already at or under the cap comes back unchanged (never enlarges); no
   returned edge is ever zero. *)
```

`Canvas_ffi` holds the hand-written `Jv` bindings for the browser calls `brr` does
not bind. It lives in the separate `nopal_image_web.internal` library and is
deliberately NOT re-exported from `Nopal_image_web`: an application calls
`process`, and calling `read_pixels` directly would carry a full-resolution image
across the boundary, bypassing the single-crossing guarantee above. Reach it as
`Nopal_image_web_internal.Canvas_ffi`, from a library you have to depend on by
name — the pipeline's own tests are the intended audience. Every canvas it
allocates is detached and never inserted into a document.

```ocaml
type Canvas_ffi.bitmap    (* a decoded image, held JavaScript-side *)
type Canvas_ffi.canvas    (* detached canvas + its pixel backing store *)
type Canvas_ffi.context   (* a canvas 2D drawing context *)

Canvas_ffi.decode  : Brr.Blob.t -> ((bitmap, string) result -> unit) -> unit
                     (* calls k exactly once; caller owns the bitmap *)
Canvas_ffi.bitmap_width  : bitmap -> int
Canvas_ffi.bitmap_height : bitmap -> int
Canvas_ffi.release       : bitmap -> unit   (* idempotent *)
Canvas_ffi.create_canvas : width:int -> height:int -> canvas
Canvas_ffi.canvas_width  : canvas -> int    (* read back off the canvas *)
Canvas_ffi.canvas_height : canvas -> int
Canvas_ffi.context_2d    : canvas -> context option   (* None, not an exception *)
Canvas_ffi.draw    : context -> bitmap -> width:int -> height:int -> unit
Canvas_ffi.encode  : canvas -> mime:string -> quality:float
                     -> ((Brr.Blob.t, string) result -> unit) -> unit
Canvas_ffi.read_pixels : context -> Brr.Tarray.uint8_clamped
                     (* whole backing store, packed RGBA, four bytes per pixel *)

(* An asynchronous rejection arrives as Error message through the continuation; a
   synchronous refusal lets the Jv.Error escape, so the caller attributes it to
   the stage that raised. Nothing here classifies a failure. Derive encode's mime
   from Config.format_to_mime on the typed variant, never from a caller string. *)
```

### Test Renderer (`nopal_test`)

Pure OCaml structural testing without a browser. The implicit-submission model
that backs the button/form rules below lives in `Implicit_submission`, in the
`nopal_test.internal` library: it is not API and carries no stability promise.

```ocaml
(* Render and inspect *)
Test_renderer.render   : 'msg Element.t -> 'msg rendered
  (* A scroll container's [reveal] declaration is surfaced as the derived attr
     pairs "reveal" and "reveal-align", appended after the view's own attrs;
     a lookup resolves to the last pair, so a declaration wins over a
     caller-supplied pair of the same name.
     Nothing marks a pair as derived, so the precedence does not run the other
     way: a container supplying ("reveal", "decoy") in attrs and declaring no
     reveal reads back attr "reveal" = Some "decoy", which is the caller's own
     attribute and not a declaration.
     A box's [focusable] declaration is surfaced the same way, as the derived
     attr "focusable" = "true"; a box that is not focusable carries no such pair
     and reads back None. Only the flag is surfaced — this renderer models no
     propagation, so the subtree scoping of a box's focus edges is not
     observable here.
     An image's [fit] is surfaced as the derived attr "fit" = "contain" or
     "cover"; an image with no fit carries no such pair and reads back None. *)
Test_renderer.tree     : 'msg rendered -> node
Test_renderer.messages : 'msg rendered -> 'msg list

(* Query *)
Test_renderer.find     : selector -> node -> node option
Test_renderer.find_all : selector -> node -> node list
Test_renderer.text_content : node -> string
Test_renderer.find_heading : Element.heading_level -> string -> node -> node option
  (* The first heading of that level, pre-order depth-first, whose text_content
     is exactly the string — a test names a heading by level and text, never by
     a tag or an ARIA pair. A heading of several runs matches on their
     concatenation. A heading node's tag is "h1" … "h6", and its attrs are the
     view's own followed by ("role", "heading"), ("aria-level", digit) and
     ("data-nopal-heading", ""). There is no heading selector constructor. *)

type selector = By_tag of string | By_text of string | By_attr of string * string
              | First_child | Nth_child of int
  (* A graphic is found by its accessible name with By_attr: a "canvas" node
     (Element.draw) carries ("role", "img") and ("aria-label", n) when Named,
     ("aria-hidden", "true") alone when Decorative; an "image" node carries
     ("alt", n), or ("alt", "") when Decorative. These are the pairs the web
     backend writes, so a test can assert a decorative graphic exposes no role
     and no aria-label. *)

(* Simulate events *)
Test_renderer.click        : selector -> 'msg rendered -> (unit, error) result
  (* A button is answered as a browser answers it: a disabled one appends
     nothing; an enabled button typed Submit inside a form appends its own
     on_click, when it has one, and then the form's on_submit, so one click can
     append two messages; a Push button appends its on_click alone. No_handler
     exactly when the click would append nothing. *)
Test_renderer.input        : selector -> string -> 'msg rendered -> (unit, error) result
Test_renderer.select_files : selector -> Element.file_info list -> 'msg rendered -> (unit, error) result
  (* File input node renders under tag "file_input", carrying accept/capture/
     multiple as node attrs only where the picker configures them — an
     unconfigured one carries no such key at all, the way the DOM carries none.
     Passing [[]] simulates clearing the picker: the handler still fires, with
     an empty list. *)
Test_renderer.submit       : selector -> 'msg rendered -> (unit, error) result
Test_renderer.submit_form  : selector -> 'msg rendered -> (unit, error) result
Test_renderer.keydown      : selector -> string -> 'msg rendered -> (unit, error) result
  (* Three simulators can reach a submit, and they are not synonyms:
     - submit pokes the selected element's own on_submit — an input's —
       directly. No on_keydown is consulted and no form is reached.
     - submit_form pokes the selected form's on_submit directly (a form renders
       under tag "form"), standing for a submission however it arose. It never
       walks: a field inside a form is not the form, and [No_handler] answers a
       non-form or a form with no on_submit. It consults no field's handlers.
     - keydown is the one that carries the submit contract: it presses a key in
       a field and follows Submit_route.of_key through the field's on_keydown,
       then its on_submit, then the nearest enclosing form. An Enter deferred
       to the form appends what the browser's implicit submission dispatches:
       with a submit button, the first in tree order is clicked — its on_click
       and then the form's on_submit, or nothing when it is disabled; with
       none, the form's on_submit when the form holds at most one input, and
       nothing when it holds more. One call appends at most two messages, and
       two only through a default button. An input with on_submit but no
       on_keydown answers Ok () rather than No_handler — the message appended
       for Enter, nothing for any other key. A test asserting which handler
       answers an Enter uses keydown; the two pokes cannot answer that.
     The platform's own share in a submission is modelled by click and
     keydown, the two simulators that press something, and by neither poke. *)
Test_renderer.dblclick     : selector -> 'msg rendered -> (unit, error) result
  (* A disabled button has no dblclick handler, so it returns No_handler and
     dispatches nothing. *)
Test_renderer.click_link   : host:Link.host -> Link.click -> selector -> 'msg rendered
  -> ('msg Link.action, error) result
  (* Answers [click] on the first matching link as a renderer for [host] would:
     the action Link.decide returns, so a test asserts "navigated in-app"
     (Ok (Navigate msg)) versus "left to the platform" (Ok Leave_to_platform)
     or "handed to the opener" (Ok (Open_externally url)). Only Navigate
     appends its message; no opener runs, so on_open_failed is never appended.
     Not_found when nothing matches, No_handler { tag; event = "click" } when
     the element is not a link. Test_renderer.click does not follow links. *)
Test_renderer.focus        : selector -> 'msg rendered -> (unit, error) result
Test_renderer.blur         : selector -> 'msg rendered -> (unit, error) result
  (* These two resolve against an input's focus edges. The box equivalents are
     box_focus/box_blur below and are distinct functions. *)
Test_renderer.box_focus    : selector -> 'msg rendered -> (unit, error) result
Test_renderer.box_blur     : selector -> 'msg rendered -> (unit, error) result
  (* Each fires the selected node's own handler and models no propagation. A real
     backend scopes a box's focus edges to its whole subtree, so focus landing on
     a descendant reaches the enclosing box and a move between two descendants of
     one box is not a leave; none of that is reproduced here. A structural test
     pins which message a box dispatches, never which node's focus caused it, and
     cannot stand in for a browser-level test of the subtree behaviour. *)
Test_renderer.pointer_move : selector -> x:float -> y:float -> 'msg rendered -> (unit, error) result
Test_renderer.pointer_leave : selector -> 'msg rendered -> (unit, error) result
Test_renderer.pointer_down : selector -> x:float -> y:float -> 'msg rendered -> (unit, error) result
Test_renderer.pointer_up   : selector -> x:float -> y:float -> 'msg rendered -> (unit, error) result
Test_renderer.draw_wheel   : selector -> delta_y:float -> x:float -> y:float -> 'msg rendered -> (unit, error) result

(* Full MVU loop testing *)
Test_renderer.run_app :
  init:(unit -> 'model * 'msg Cmd.t) ->
  update:('model -> 'msg -> 'model * 'msg Cmd.t) ->
  view:('model -> 'msg Element.t) ->
  'msg list -> 'model * 'msg rendered
```

**Attribute answers that moved — read this on a pin bump.** The structural
renderer now resolves an attribute the way the browser does, and that moves
what it answers on seven `(node tag, key)` pairs. Every signature is unchanged,
so a downstream structural suite meets this with no compiler help. The "before"
column is the tree at commit `b74a21d`, where a derived pair was prepended, a
lookup resolved to the first pair, and a pair was emitted for a key even where
the typed field asserted nothing.

| # | Node tag | Key | When | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `checkbox` | `disabled` | the control is not disabled (the default) | `Some "false"` | the view's own last pair for that key, else `None` |
| 2 | `radio` | `disabled` | the control is not disabled (the default) | `Some "false"` | the view's own last pair for that key, else `None` |
| 3 | `select` | `disabled` | the control is not disabled (the default) | `Some "false"` | the view's own last pair for that key, else `None` |
| 4 | `option` (a select's generated child) | `disabled` | that option is not disabled (the default) | `Some "false"` | `None` — option children carry no caller attrs, so there is nothing to uncover |
| 5 | `file_input` | `accept` | `?accept` is `[]` (the default) | `Some ""` | the view's own last pair for that key, else `None` |
| 6 | `file_input` | `capture` | no `?capture` (the default) | `Some ""` | the view's own last pair for that key, else `None` |
| 7 | `file_input` | `multiple` | `?multiple` is false (the default) | `Some "false"` | the view's own last pair for that key, else `None` |

Where the typed field does assert — `~disabled:true`, a non-empty `~accept`, a
`~capture`, `~multiple:true` — nothing moved: the value is unchanged and the
derivation still wins the key. For a node whose view declared no pair of that
name, each of the seven also moves `has_attr` from `true` to `false`, and a
`By_attr (key, "false")` or `By_attr ("capture", "")` selector that matched that
node now matches nothing.

Keys that did **not** move, recorded so a reader does not go looking: `checked`,
`value`, `selected`, `label`, `name`, `placeholder`, `focusable`, `reveal`,
`reveal-align`. Each is either unconditional and still unconditional, or was
already conditional before this change.

Two further changes travel with the seven and move no key's answer:

8. **Every resolution point agrees.** Last-wins now governs not only `attr` and
   `find`/`find_all` but also the selector `click`, `input`, `submit` and
   `select_files` resolve. A suite selecting `By_attr` on a key its own view
   spells twice reaches the node on the last pair and no longer reaches it on
   the first. The dispatch path is covered — `by_attr_matches_the_resolved_value`
   clicks `By_attr ("data-role", …)` on a button whose view spells that key
   twice and asserts both outcomes — but the compiler cannot see the change, so
   a downstream suite meets it with no help. (`has_attr` is presence only and is
   not governed by last-wins; it answers `true` whichever pair won.)

9. **Node `attrs` list order.** A derived pair used to sit at the front of a
   node's `attrs` list and now sits at the back, on every arm that derives one:
   `box` (`focusable`), `input` (`value`, `placeholder`), `checkbox`
   (`checked`), `radio` (`name`, `checked`), `select` (`selected`), `option`
   (`value`, `label`), `file_input` (`accept`, `capture`, `multiple`) and
   `scroll` (`reveal`, `reveal-align`). `node` exposes `attrs` publicly, so a
   whole-list equality on a node sees a different list even where every lookup
   on it answers the same.

**Submit and form answers that moved — read this on a pin bump.**
The submit contract (under *Element DSL*) and the new `Form` arm move nine
answers a downstream consumer can meet. Rows 1–5 compile unchanged, so a
downstream suite or app meets them with no compiler help; rows 6–9 are
compile-visible. "Before" is the tree at commit `1fd1cad`. The pin in
`test/unit/nopal_test/test_test_renderer.ml` (`change_list`) covers the
candidate keys the test lists, not this whole table: rows 6–9 are
compile-visible and pinned by construction (their "before" is "does not
compile"); rows 2–3 are read from `Submit_route.of_key` rather than the web
renderer, since exercising the web half needs a browser. Within that
candidate set, a key that moved and is not a row, or a row whose answer did
not move, fails it.

| # | Key | When | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `enter-declined-by-on-keydown-reaches-on-submit` | Enter in an input carrying **both** `on_keydown` and `on_submit`, where `on_keydown` returns `None` for Enter | browser: nothing dispatched — supplying `on_keydown` installed no `on_submit` listener at all; `Test_renderer.keydown`: `Ok ()`, nothing appended | `on_submit` is dispatched, in both renderers |
| 2 | `enter-consumed-by-on-keydown-prevents-default` | Enter in an input whose `on_keydown` returns `Some msg` for it | `msg` dispatched; the key's default left alone | `msg` dispatched and the default prevented, so an enclosing form does not also submit (browser only; the structural renderer models no default at `1fd1cad`; implicit submission is now modelled, see Button answers that moved) |
| 3 | `enter-answered-by-on-submit-prevents-default` | Enter in an input whose own `on_submit` answers it | `on_submit` dispatched; the default left alone | `on_submit` dispatched and the default prevented (browser only) |
| 4 | `keydown-enter-on-an-input-with-only-on-submit` | `Test_renderer.keydown sel "Enter"` on an input with `on_submit` and no `on_keydown` | `Error (No_handler _)` | `Ok ()`, `on_submit` appended |
| 5 | `keydown-other-key-on-an-input-with-only-on-submit` | `Test_renderer.keydown sel k`, `k` not Enter, on the same input | `Error (No_handler _)` | `Ok ()`, nothing appended |
| 6 | `element-t-gains-form` | any exhaustive `match` on `Element.t` | compiles | fails to compile until it handles `Form { … }` — the new arm, rendered under tag `"form"` |
| 7 | `input-gains-required` | an input passing `~required:true` beside an `("required", _)` pair in `~attrs` | the argument does not exist | the typed field wins: the pair stops taking effect (`"true"` structurally, a presence attribute in the DOM), with `aria-required` alongside |
| 8 | `input-gains-autocomplete` | an input passing `~autocomplete` beside an `("autocomplete", _)` pair | the argument does not exist | the typed field wins; the pair stops taking effect |
| 9 | `input-gains-input_type` | an input passing `~input_type` beside a `("type", _)` pair | the argument does not exist | the typed field wins; the pair stops taking effect |

Rows 6–9 also break code that builds or destructures the `Input` record
directly: it gains `required`, `autocomplete` and `input_type` fields, so an
`Input { … }` pattern listing its fields without `; _` stops compiling. An
`open Nopal_element.Element` brings the new constructors `On`, `Off`,
`Password`, `Email`, `Tel`, `Url`, `Number`, `Search` and `Plain` into scope
(see `Element.input`).

What did **not** move, recorded so a reader does not go looking — the test pins
each as unchanged: an `on_keydown` consuming Enter beside an `on_submit` (the
keydown's message, and only it); an Enter an `on_keydown` declines with no
`on_submit` and no form (nothing); a consuming `on_keydown` on any other key
(dispatched, default kept); `keydown` on an input with no handler
(`No_handler`); `Test_renderer.submit` on an input's `on_submit`; and an input
that authors none of the three new arguments — its `("required", _)`,
`("autocomplete", _)` and `("type", _)` pairs stand exactly as before. Existing
`Element.input` call sites compile untouched.

For a consumer that deliberately supplied only `on_submit` because supplying
`on_keydown` suppressed it, that workaround stops being necessary: both
handlers can now be supplied together, and row 1 is what changes when they are.

**Button answers that moved — read this on a pin bump.**
**Every complete `Nopal_ui.Button.config` record literal stops compiling.** The
record gains a `button_type` field (row 1), and the compiler says `Error: Some
record fields are undefined: button_type`. Add `button_type = Push` to keep the
button from submitting, or `button_type = Submit` for the one button that
should submit its form. A config built with `Button.default` and the `with_*`
setters compiles untouched; `Button.with_button_type` is the supported route.

`Element.button` gains a typed `button_type` and a typed `disabled`, and a
button that names no type no longer submits its form. That moves the fourteen
answers below. Rows 1–2 are compile-visible; rows 3–14 are silent, so a
downstream suite or app meets them with no compiler help. "Before" is the tree
at commit `80ec712`. The Where column names the renderer whose answer moved:
the browser, the structural `Test_renderer`, or both. The pins are `change_list`
in `test/unit/nopal_test/test_test_renderer.ml`, for every row whose key does
not start `ui-button-`, and `test/unit/nopal_ui/test_change_list.ml`, for the
rows whose key does. Each reads this table, and within its candidate keys a key
that moved and is not a row, or a row whose answer did not move, fails it. A
browser row is read through the structural renderer, which
`test/e2e/fixtures/button-submit-matrix.tsv` holds equal to Chromium cell by
cell.

| # | Key | Visible | Where | When | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ui-button-config-gains-button_type` | compile | both | a complete `Nopal_ui.Button.config` record literal | compiles | fails to compile until it supplies `button_type` |
| 2 | `element-button-record-gains-fields` | compile | both | a `Button { … }` pattern listing its fields without `; _`, or code building that record directly | compiles | fails to compile until it handles `button_type` and `disabled` |
| 3 | `button-renders-type-button` | silent | both | an `Element.button` or `Nopal_ui.Button` that names no type, including `Navigation_bar`'s tab buttons, `Bottom_tabs`'s back affordance, `Data_table`'s sort controls, and `Toast`'s dismiss button, all of which render `E.button` and now stop submitting an enclosing `Form` | no `type` attribute; `attr "type"` is `None` | `type="button"` in the DOM; `attr "type"` is `Some "button"` |
| 4 | `untyped-button-in-form-does-not-submit` | silent | browser | clicking a button that names no type inside a `Form` with `on_submit` | its `on_click`, then the form's `on_submit` | its `on_click` alone (the structural renderer already answered this) |
| 5 | `enter-with-only-untyped-buttons` | silent | browser | Enter in a field of a form whose only buttons name no type | the first button's `on_click`, then the form's `on_submit` | two or more inputs: nothing; one input: the form's `on_submit` alone |
| 6 | `attrs-type-pair-on-button-overruled` | silent | both | a `("type", _)` pair in a button's `~attrs`, or in `Nopal_ui.Button`'s `attrs` | the pair's value, so `("type", "submit")` made the button submit | the typed `button_type` wins: `"button"` unless the button is typed `Submit`, so a `("type", "submit")` pair stops submitting |
| 7 | `click-submit-button-reaches-form` | silent | structural | `Test_renderer.click` on an enabled submit button inside a form with `on_submit` | the button's `on_click` alone, or `Error (No_handler _)` with no `on_click` | its `on_click`, then the form's `on_submit`; with no `on_click`, `Ok ()` and the form's `on_submit` alone |
| 8 | `keydown-enter-multi-field-no-submit-button` | silent | structural | `Test_renderer.keydown sel "Enter"` on a bare input in a form with two or more inputs and no submit button | `Ok ()`, the form's `on_submit` appended | `Error (No_handler _)`, nothing appended |
| 9 | `keydown-enter-enabled-default-button` | silent | structural | the same Enter in a form whose first submit button is enabled | the form's `on_submit` | the button's `on_click`, then the form's `on_submit`: one `keydown` can now append two messages |
| 10 | `keydown-enter-disabled-default-button` | silent | structural | the same Enter in a form whose first submit button is disabled | the form's `on_submit` | `Error (No_handler _)`, nothing appended, even when an enabled submit button follows |
| 11 | `ui-button-disabled-or-loading-in-form` | silent | both | a disabled or loading `Nopal_ui.Button` that is its form's submit button (at `80ec712`, any `Button` in a form): a click on it, or an Enter in a field | the form's `on_submit`, for both | nothing, for both |
| 12 | `ui-button-loading-gains-aria-disabled` | silent | both | a loading `Nopal_ui.Button` that is not disabled | no `aria-disabled` | `aria-disabled="true"`, beside `aria-busy="true"` |
| 13 | `ui-button-aria-disabled-pair-overruled` | silent | both | a disabled or loading `Nopal_ui.Button` with an `("aria-disabled", _)` pair in `config.attrs` | the caller's value | `"true"`: the derived value wins while the button is inert |
| 14 | `disabled-button-dblclick-dispatches-nothing` | silent | both | `dblclick` (browser or `Test_renderer.dblclick`) on a disabled button carrying `on_dblclick` | — (no disabled state existed) | `Error No_handler`, nothing dispatched — a disabled button is inert on every route, dblclick included |

To keep a button submitting its form, type it: `~button_type:Submit` on
`Element.button`, or `Button.with_button_type Submit`. A `("type", "submit")`
pair no longer does it, and nothing reports that it stopped. A disabled
`Element.button` (`~disabled:true`, new) renders `aria-disabled="true"` and not
the native `disabled` attribute, so it stays focusable and in the tab order; a
caller who wants the native attribute can still spell it through `~attrs`, but
that route is outside the structural model: the browser treats such a button
as disabled, while the structural renderer answers it as enabled. An
`open Nopal_element.Element` brings the new constructors `Submit` and `Push`
into scope, where they can shadow a message constructor of the same name.

What did **not** move, recorded so a reader does not go looking — the two pins
hold each as unchanged. Existing `Element.button` call sites compile untouched.
Outside a form a button's type has no effect: clicking an enabled button
dispatches its `on_click`, and one with no `on_click` answers `No_handler`,
exactly as before. A `("type", "button")` pair reads `"button"`, as it did. An
enabled button leaves a caller's `("aria-disabled", _)` pair standing. Enter in
a form holding a single input and no button submits it, and Enter that the
input's own `on_submit` answers dispatches that message alone, even with a
submit button in the form. `Test_renderer.submit_form` pokes the form's
`on_submit` as before. On `Nopal_ui.Button`: a disabled button carries
`aria-disabled="true"` and a loading one `aria-busy="true"`, as before; a
caller's `("aria-busy", _)` pair on a loading button still wins; an enabled
button's click outside a form dispatches its `on_click` and a disabled one's
dispatches nothing; and an enabled `Button` given `with_button_type Submit`
answers a click and an Enter in its form exactly as an untyped one did at
`80ec712` — its `on_click`, then the form's `on_submit`. The `disabled` of
`Element.checkbox`, `radio` and `select` is untouched and is still the native
attribute.

**Link answers that moved — read this on a pin bump.**
**Every exhaustive `match` on `Element.t` stops compiling** (row 1): the
variant gains a `Link` arm, and the compiler reports the missing case
(warning 8, an error under dune's default dev profile). Handle `Link { child;
_ }` the way the match handles a single-child container such as `Button`.
**A Tauri app that mounts through `Nopal_web.mount` stops mounting** (row 2):
it compiles, and at run time the window shows a refusal instead of the app.
Mount through `Nopal_tauri_mount` instead, and add the three host edits
(row 12) or every external link answers `Not_permitted`.

Everything else is additive. "Before" is the tree at commit `c2ef9ea`. No test
reads this table.

| # | Key | Visible | Who meets it | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `element-t-gains-link-arm` | compile | any exhaustive `match` on `Element.t` (a renderer, a tree walker, a test helper) | the match is exhaustive | non-exhaustive until it handles `Link of { style; interaction; attrs; destination : 'msg Link.destination; child }` |
| 2 | `nopal-web-mount-refuses-on-tauri` | run time | a Tauri app calling `Nopal_web.mount` or `mount_with_telemetry` without `~open_external` (the page defines `__TAURI_INTERNALS__`) | mounts and runs | no runtime and no app: the fault text (Web Renderer → `Nopal_web.mount`, below) is written into the target and sent to `?on_error`, and `unmount` is inert. `mount_with_telemetry` runs the app's `init`, installs no bridge, and returns a handle that records nothing. `nopal_web` reads that one global and depends on no Tauri package |
| 3 | `nopal-web-mount-gains-open-external` | compile, rarely | code annotating `Nopal_web.mount`'s or `mount_with_telemetry`'s full type | no `?open_external` | `?open_external:(Url.t -> ((unit, Link.open_error) result -> unit) -> unit)`; given, links render for `Link.Webview`, omitted, for `Link.Browser`. Ordinary call sites compile untouched |
| 4 | `nopal-tauri-mount` | additive | a Tauri app | no Tauri mount entry point; the app chose `?write_clipboard` itself | library `nopal_tauri.mount`, module `Nopal_tauri_mount`, with `mount` and `mount_with_telemetry`: the `Nopal_web` arguments minus `?write_clipboard` and `?open_external`, which it supplies |
| 5 | `nopal-tauri-package-depends-on-nopal-web` | install | anyone installing the `nopal_tauri` opam package | no `nopal_web` dependency | depends on `nopal_web` (for the sub-library). The `nopal_tauri` library itself still links no UI package |
| 6 | `element-link-builder` | additive | view code | no link element | `Element.link : ?style -> ?interaction -> ?attrs -> 'msg Link.destination -> 'msg Element.t -> 'msg Element.t`, rendered as tag `a` by both renderers |
| 7 | `link-href-rel-typed` | silent | a link's `~attrs` | — | `href` is always derived (the path or the URL), so an `("href", _)` pair never takes effect; `rel` is `"noopener noreferrer"` on `External` and absent on `Route`, so a `("rel", _)` pair stands on a `Route` link only |
| 8 | `nopal-element-new-modules` | compile, rarely | code doing `open Nopal_element` that has its own `Url`, `Route_path` or `Link` module | not in scope | `Url`, `Route_path` and `Link` are in scope and can shadow a same-named module |
| 9 | `router-destination` | additive | routed apps | no way to derive a link from a route | `Router.destination : 'route t -> 'route -> on_follow:('route -> 'msg) -> ('msg Link.destination, Route_path.error) result`: the path is exactly `push`'s string, a refusal is returned and never defaulted, and it does not navigate. `nopal_platform` now names `nopal_element` in its dune `libraries` (it was already a transitive dependency) |
| 10 | `test-renderer-click-link` | additive | structural tests | no link to click | `Test_renderer.click_link : host:Link.host -> Link.click -> selector -> 'msg rendered -> ('msg Link.action, error) result`, appending the message on `Navigate` only. `Test_renderer.click` does not follow links |
| 11 | `nopal-tauri-opener` | additive | Tauri apps; code doing `open Nopal_tauri` that has its own `Opener` module | — | `Nopal_tauri.Opener.open_url : Url.t -> ((unit, Link.open_error) result -> unit) -> unit`, resolving once, with the URL replaced by `<url>` in every `Failed` reason |
| 12 | `tauri-host-opener-plugin` | run time | the Tauri host project (`src-tauri`) | no opener plugin | `tauri-plugin-opener = "2"` in `Cargo.toml`, `.plugin(tauri_plugin_opener::init())` in `src/lib.rs`, and `"opener:allow-open-url"` plus `"opener:allow-default-urls"` in `capabilities/default.json`, not `opener:default`. Without the plugin registered, or without either permission line, an external link click dispatches `on_open_failed Not_permitted` |
| 13 | `renderer-link-host` | compile, rarely | code using `Nopal_web.Renderer` directly, or doing `open Nopal_web.Renderer` | — | new `type opener`, `type link_host = Browser \| Webview of { open_external : opener }`, and `create ?link_host` (default `Browser`); the open brings constructors `Browser` and `Webview` into scope |
| 14 | `kitchen-sink-main-mounts-tauri` | example | anyone copying the kitchen sink's `main.ml` | `Nopal_web.mount* ?write_clipboard`, selected by `has_tauri ()` | `Nopal_tauri_mount.mount*` when `has_tauri ()`, `Nopal_web.mount*` otherwise; no local clipboard selection |

What did **not** move: no existing element's rendered tree, and no existing
signature other than the two mounts' new optional argument. A browser app
mounting through `Nopal_web.mount` behaves exactly as before. `Router.push`,
`Router.on_navigate` (popstate only) and `Runtime.create` are unchanged.

**Text_input answers that moved — read this on a pin bump.**
**Every complete `Nopal_ui.TextInput.config` record literal stops compiling**
(rows 1–6). The record gains `required`, `autocomplete`, `input_type`, `name`,
`on_keydown` and `on_focus`, and the compiler says `Error: Some record fields
are undefined: …`. Add the listed fields as `None` to keep every answer as it
was. A config built with `TextInput.make` and the `with_*` setters, or updated
with `{ config with … }`, compiles untouched; each new field has a setter, and
the setter is the supported route. No existing field, `make` or `with_*`
signature changed.

`Element.input` gains a typed `name` (rows 7–8), and a `Text_input` with an
error is now announced as invalid (row 9). Rows 10–14 are the `config.attrs`
pairs a caller can now replace with a setter, or drop. "Before" is the tree at
commit `0a56b7f`. The Where column names the renderer whose answer moved: the
browser, the structural `Test_renderer`, or both. No test reads this table.
Row 9, and the unchanged answer without an error, are pinned in both directions
by the hand-kept lists in `test/unit/nopal_ui/test_change_list.ml`, which are
edited together with it. Rows 1–7 are compile-visible. Rows 8 and 10–14 are
joined to this text by nothing: the behaviour each describes is tested, but an
edit to the text alone reddens no test.

| # | Key | Visible | Where | When | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ui-text-input-config-gains-required` | compile | both | a complete `Nopal_ui.TextInput.config` record literal | compiles | fails to compile until it supplies `required`; `None` derives nothing, and `with_required` sets it |
| 2 | `ui-text-input-config-gains-autocomplete` | compile | both | the same literal | compiles | fails to compile until it supplies `autocomplete`; `with_autocomplete` sets it |
| 3 | `ui-text-input-config-gains-input_type` | compile | both | the same literal | compiles | fails to compile until it supplies `input_type`; `with_input_type` sets it |
| 4 | `ui-text-input-config-gains-name` | compile | both | the same literal | compiles | fails to compile until it supplies `name`; `with_name` sets it |
| 5 | `ui-text-input-config-gains-on_keydown` | compile | both | the same literal | compiles | fails to compile until it supplies `on_keydown`; `with_on_keydown` sets it |
| 6 | `ui-text-input-config-gains-on_focus` | compile | both | the same literal | compiles | fails to compile until it supplies `on_focus`; `with_on_focus` sets it |
| 7 | `element-input-record-gains-name` | compile | both | an `Input { … }` pattern listing its fields without `; _`, or code building that record directly | compiles | fails to compile until it handles `name : string option` |
| 8 | `element-input-gains-name` | additive | both | an input passing `~name`, or a `Text_input` given `with_name`, beside a `("name", _)` pair in its attrs | the argument does not exist | the typed field wins and the pair stops taking effect. With no `~name` the pair stands, and once neither is present the browser removes the attribute on the next render |
| 9 | `ui-text-input-aria-invalid` | silent | both | a `Text_input` whose `config.error` is `Some _` | absent, unless a caller's `("aria-invalid", _)` pair in `config.attrs` supplied it | `aria-invalid="true"`, as a pair ahead of `config.attrs`, so a caller's pair still replaces it. With `config.error = None` nothing is derived, as before |
| 10 | `ui-text-input-replace-type-pair` | migration | both | a `Text_input` carrying `("type", t)` in `config.attrs` | the pair was the only route | `with_input_type`, with `Plain` for `"text"`. A kind `input_type` does not name keeps the pair, which stands while no `with_input_type` is set |
| 11 | `ui-text-input-replace-autocomplete-pair` | migration | both | a `Text_input` carrying `("autocomplete", v)` in `config.attrs` | the pair was the only route | `with_autocomplete v` |
| 12 | `ui-text-input-replace-required-pair` | migration | both | a `Text_input` carrying `("required", "")` in `config.attrs` | `required` from the pair, and no `aria-required` | `with_required true`, which also brings `aria-required="true"`. Structurally `required` then reads `"true"` rather than the pair's `""` |
| 13 | `ui-text-input-replace-name-pair` | migration | both | a `Text_input` carrying `("name", v)` in `config.attrs` | the pair was the only route | `with_name v` |
| 14 | `ui-text-input-drop-aria-invalid-pair` | migration | both | a `Text_input` carrying `("aria-invalid", "true")` in `config.attrs`, set while `config.error` is `Some _` | the pair was the only route | drop the pair: row 9 derives the same answer. A pair set while `config.error` is `None` still stands, and is still the only route there |

A pair from rows 10–13 kept beside its setter does nothing: the typed field
outranks it. Disabled suppression now also covers `on_focus` and `on_keydown`,
on the same terms as `on_change`, `on_submit` and `on_blur`. Both handlers are
new, so no answer an existing caller meets moves.

**A node's `attrs` list.** With an error, the input's list gains
`("aria-invalid", "true")` directly after `aria-describedby`, ahead of
`config.attrs`. An input given any of the four new typed fields gains that
field's derived pairs at the back of the list. Every lookup answers as the
table says, but `Test_renderer.node` exposes `attrs` publicly, so a whole-list
equality on that node sees a different list.

What did **not** move, recorded so a reader does not go looking. The input's
`aria-describedby` is still `error_id config` with an error and absent without
one. Its `id`, `aria-labelledby` and `data-field` answer as they did at
`0a56b7f`. `test_change_list.ml` holds `aria-describedby` and `data-field` as
unchanged, and the naming cases in `test/unit/nopal_ui/test_text_input.ml` hold
`id` and `aria-labelledby`. A `Text_input` with no error that uses none of the
new setters renders exactly the tree it did. Existing `Element.input` call sites
compile untouched. `Checkbox`, `Radio_group` and `Select_input` are untouched:
each already passed every field of the element it wraps.

**Arc answers that moved — read this on a pin bump.**
**Every complete `Arc_to { … }` record literal, and every `Arc_to` pattern
that lists its fields without `; _`, stops compiling** (row 1). The constructor
gains a required `direction : direction` field (`Clockwise | Anticlockwise`) in
`Nopal_scene.Path`, which `Nopal_draw.Path` re-exports. A literal is rejected
for the missing field; a closed pattern trips warning 9, an error under dune's
default dev profile. Write `direction = Clockwise` to keep a literal's canvas
reading, and handle both constructors in a pattern. **Every call to
`Nopal_draw.Path.arc_to`, `arc_segment` or `donut_arc` needs a trailing `()`**
(row 3): without it the call is a partial application, and the type error is
reported where the result is used. A call with no `~direction` still draws
clockwise.

"Before" is the tree at commit `fd02c03`. The Where column names the renderer
whose answer moved: canvas, SVG, or both. No test reads this table. The
behaviour each row describes is tested, by the one edge-case table that
generates both the canvas and the SVG suites or by the kitchen sink's donut
pixel checks, but an edit to the text alone reddens no test.

| # | Key | Visible | Where | When | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `scene-path-arc-to-gains-direction` | compile | both | a complete `Arc_to { … }` literal, or an `Arc_to` pattern listing its fields without `; _` | five float fields | fails to compile until it supplies or handles `direction : direction` |
| 2 | `scene-path-arc-to-requires-direction` | compile | both | a call to `Nopal_scene.Path.arc_to` | `~cx ~cy ~r ~start_angle ~end_angle` | also requires `~direction`; this layer has no default |
| 3 | `draw-path-arc-builders-end-in-unit` | compile | both | a call to `Nopal_draw.Path.arc_to`, `arc_segment` or `donut_arc` | ended at `~end_angle`; `Nopal_draw.Path.arc_to` was the scene builder, re-exported | `?direction … ~end_angle ()`, with `?direction` defaulting to `Clockwise`; add `()` to every call |
| 4 | `draw-arc-module` | compile, rarely | both | code doing `open Nopal_draw` that has its own `Arc` module | not in scope | `Nopal_draw.Arc` is in scope and can shadow it: `type resolved = Invalid \| Sweep of { start : float; sweep : float }` and `resolve`, the shared sweep rules ("Arc rules" under 2D Drawing) |
| 5 | `draw-donut-arc-inner-edge-reverses` | render | both | `donut_arc` | the inner arc ran from `end_angle` back to `start_angle` with no direction, so each renderer read it its own way | the inner arc carries the opposite of `?direction`, so `Anticlockwise` by default |
| 6 | `pie-donut-hole-empty` | render | both | `Pie.scene` or `Pie.view` with `~inner_radius` above `0.` | canvas: the hole filled with the segment's colour; SVG: chord slivers of the segment's colour in the hole | the hole is empty and shows whatever lies behind the chart |
| 7 | `svg-arc-continues-subpath` | bytes, render | SVG | `Svg_fmt.path_to_d`, and so `Nopal_svg.render`, on an `Arc_to` that follows an open subpath | `M x y` to the arc's start, opening a second subpath | `L x y`: `arc_segment ~cx:50. ~cy:40. ~r:30. ~start_angle:0. ~end_angle:(π/2) ()` gives `M 80 40 L 80 40 C 80 56.5685 66.5685 70 50 70` where it gave `M 80 40 M 80 40 C …`. When the pen is not already on the arc's start, the render changes too: the old `M` lifted the pen and left the earlier subpath unjoined, and the `L` now draws a connecting line (and fills across it). An arc with no open subpath still opens with `M` |
| 8 | `svg-decreasing-clockwise-arc-long-way` | render | SVG | an arc whose end angle is below its start angle, with `Clockwise`, the default of every `Nopal_draw` builder | the short way round: SVG swept the signed `end_angle - start_angle` | the long way round, as canvas always drew it: `arc_segment … ~start_angle:π ~end_angle:(π/2) ()` gives three curves where it gave one. Pass `~direction:Anticlockwise` for the short way |
| 9 | `svg-invalid-or-empty-arc` | bytes | SVG | an invalid arc (a non-finite centre, radius or angle, or a negative radius), or an arc with a zero sweep | invalid: `M nan nan C …`, or an arc reflected through the centre; zero sweep: a `C` with NaN control points | invalid: nothing at all; zero sweep: only the `L` or `M` to its start point |
| 10 | `canvas-arc-anticlockwise` | render | canvas | an `Arc_to` with `Anticlockwise` | every arc ran clockwise: `arc()` was called without `anticlockwise` | `arc()` receives `anticlockwise` from the direction |
| 11 | `canvas-arc-angles-resolved` | render | canvas | a `Clockwise` arc from `2π` down to `0` | `arc()` received the raw angles, and Chromium drew a full circle | `arc()` receives `start_angle` and `start_angle` plus the resolved sweep, so that arc draws nothing, as in SVG |
| 12 | `canvas-invalid-arc-no-call` | run time | canvas | an invalid arc | passed raw to `arc()`, which threw `IndexSizeError` on a negative radius and did nothing on a non-finite value | no `arc()` call: the arc adds nothing, and the pen stays where it was |
| 13 | `nopal-svg-depends-on-nopal-draw` | install | — | anyone installing the `nopal_svg` opam package | depends on `nopal_scene` only | also depends on `nopal_draw` (and transitively `nopal_style`), which is platform-free; `nopal_svg` still builds native |
| 14 | `kitchen-sink-donut-section` | example | both | anyone copying the kitchen sink | — | a new section, `Sub_donut`, draws a multi-segment donut and a single-segment full-turn donut over a checkerboard, on a canvas and as `Nopal_svg.render` output loaded into an image; the kitchen sink library now also links `nopal_fs_key` |
| 15 | `svg-leading-move-for-line-and-curves` | bytes | SVG | `Svg_fmt.path_to_d` on a `Line_to`, `Bezier_to` or `Quad_to` with no current subpath, e.g. a path opening with one of them or following an `Invalid` arc | bare `L x y`, `C …` or `Q …` | a `Line_to` becomes a move to its point (`M x y`); a `Bezier_to` or `Quad_to` is preceded by an `M` to its first control point (the control point for `Quad_to`), matching canvas |

What did **not** move, with the one exception of row 15. An increasing arc of less than a full turn draws the
same pixels on canvas: the kitchen sink's stroked `arc_segment` demo (`0` to
`3π/2`) was compared with `fd02c03`'s build at device pixel ratios 1 and 2, and
no pixel differed. In SVG such an arc keeps its Bézier curves byte for byte, when the pen
already sits on the arc's start; otherwise only its leading command changes, as
rows 7 and 15 say. `Circle` nodes, and every
segment other than `Arc_to`, render as they did in both renderers, except a
`Line_to`, `Bezier_to` or `Quad_to` with no current subpath (row 15). `Pie` fills
without a stroke, so a full-turn donut shows no radial seam.

**Graphic answers that moved — read this on a pin bump.**
**Every call to `Element.draw`, `Element.image`, `Nopal_svg.render` and the
nine chart views stops compiling** (rows 2–3 and 5–14): each now requires
`~name:Graphic_name.t`, and there is no default. The one-line fix is to add
`~name` built from `Graphic_name.named "…"`, or `~name:Graphic_name.decorative`
for a graphic that carries no meaning of its own (a sparkline beside the number
it plots). `?aria_label` on `draw` and `~alt` on `image` are removed, not kept
beside the name: a `~alt:""` becomes `~name:Graphic_name.decorative`, and an
`~alt:" "` has no spelling, because `Graphic_name.named` refuses an empty or
blank string (ASCII whitespace, C0 controls, DEL only) with `Blank { input }`. **Every `Element.t`
pattern or literal naming `Draw`'s `aria_label` or `Image`'s `alt` stops
compiling** (row 4).

"Before" is the tree at commit `0327683`. The Where column names the renderer
whose answer moved: web, the structural `Test_renderer`, or SVG. Rows 15–19 are
the only accessibility attributes these routes derive; no other is written. No
test reads this table. The behaviour each row describes is tested in its
renderer's suite and, for web, by the kitchen-sink Playwright and axe cases, but
an edit to the text alone reddens no test.

| # | Key | Visible | Where | When | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `graphic-name-module` | compile, rarely | all | code doing `open Nopal_element` or `open Nopal_scene` that has its own `Graphic_name` module | not in scope | `Graphic_name` is in scope and can shadow it: `type t = private Named of string \| Decorative`, `type error = Blank of { input : string }`, `named`, `decorative`, `equal`, `aria_attrs`, `image_alt`. `Nopal_element.Graphic_name` is an alias of `Nopal_scene.Graphic_name`, so the types are equal |

What did **not** move, recorded so a reader does not go looking.
`Chart_pane.view`, `Chart_compose.compose` and `Legend.view` take no name:
each pane's chart is already named by its own view, and a legend is text. Every
`*.scene` function, `Canvas_renderer.render` and `nopal_image_web`'s
`Canvas_ffi.draw` are unchanged. The `Test_renderer` selectors are unchanged;
`By_attr ("aria-label", n)` finds a named canvas. A canvas located by
`canvas[aria-label='…']` still matches when given that name.

**Font answers that moved — read this on a pin bump.**
**Every exhaustive `match` on `Font.family` stops compiling** (row 1): the type
gains four constructors, `Ui_sans_serif`, `Ui_serif`, `Ui_monospace` and
`Ui_rounded`, and the missing arms trip warning 8, an error under dune's
default dev profile. **Every read of `Text.t`'s `font_family` field, and every
`font_family = Some f` record literal, stops compiling** (row 2): the field is
now `Text.font option`, so `Some f` becomes `Some (Single f)` and a match
handles `Single` and `Stack`. **Every complete `Text.t` record literal stops
compiling** (row 3) for the new `underline_offset` field; add
`underline_offset = None`. A `font_family = None` literal and every call to the
`Text.font_family` builder compile unchanged, and for a name holding none of
the characters in row 7 they emit the same bytes as before.

"Before" is the tree at commit `3ac6770`. The Where column names the output
whose answer moved: web (the CSS the DOM backend writes, inline and in class
rules), canvas, SVG, or all of them. No test reads this table. The behaviour
each row describes is tested in `nopal_style`'s `Font` and `Text` suites, the
web `Style_css` suite, the `nopal_svg` suite and the kitchen-sink Playwright
cases, but an edit to the text alone reddens no test.

| # | Key | Visible | Where | When | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `font-family-ui-constructors` | compile | all | an exhaustive `match` on `Font.family` | five constructors | nine: `Ui_sans_serif`, `Ui_serif`, `Ui_monospace`, `Ui_rounded` added, serialised as the bare keywords `ui-sans-serif`, `ui-serif`, `ui-monospace`, `ui-rounded`. Fix: add the four arms. They are not `Font.Generic.t` values and cannot end a stack |
| 2 | `text-t-font-family-field-type` | compile | all | a read of `Text.t.font_family`, or a `font_family = Some f` literal or pattern | `font_family : Font.family option` | `font_family : Text.font option`, with `type font = Single of Font.family \| Stack of Font.stack`. Fix: `Some f` becomes `Some (Single f)`; a match handles both arms. `= None` literals and `Text.font_family` calls compile |
| 3 | `text-t-underline-offset-field` | compile | all | a complete `Text.t` record literal | no such field | `underline_offset : float option`. Fix: add `underline_offset = None`. `Text.equal` compares it with `Float.equal` |
| 4 | `font-stack` | additive | all | `Nopal_style.Font` | — | `module Generic` (`type t = System_ui \| Sans_serif \| Serif \| Monospace`, `to_family`), abstract `type stack`, `stack : family list -> last_resort:Generic.t -> stack`, `families`, `equal_stack`, `stack_to_css_string`. A stack with no last resort is a type error |
| 5 | `text-font-stack` | additive | web | `Nopal_style.Text` | — | `type font`, `font_stack : Font.stack -> t -> t`, `equal_font`. The web backend emits a stack as one `font-family` declaration in order, last resort last: `"Geist", system-ui, sans-serif` |
| 6 | `text-underline-offset` | additive | web | `Nopal_style.Text` | — | `underline_offset : float -> t -> t`. The web backend emits `text-underline-offset:<n>px` (`3.0` gives `3px`, `-2.0` gives `-2px`) inline and in interaction rules; a non-finite value emits nothing. Inert on canvas and SVG |
| 7 | `css-custom-name-escaped` | bytes | web | a `Custom` name holding `"`, `\`, `{`, `}`, `;` or a control character, in a `font-family` declaration | quoted, unescaped: the name could end the string, add a declaration or, in a class rule, end the rule and start another | quoted, with `"` and `\` backslash-escaped and `{`, `}`, `;` and U+0000–U+001F, U+007F as a lowercase hex escape plus one space (`\7b `, `\7d `, `\3b `, `\a ` for LF). `Custom "Inter"` is still `"Inter"` |
| 8 | `canvas-custom-name-escaped` | bytes | canvas | `Scene.text ~font_family:(Custom n)` drawn by the canvas backend | `n` quoted, unescaped, inside the `font` shorthand | the row 7 bytes inside the `font` shorthand (`<weight> <size>px <family>`) |
| 9 | `svg-font-family-attr-escaped` | bytes | SVG | every `Scene.text` with a `Custom` family rendered by `Nopal_svg.render` | the CSS string written raw into the attribute: `font-family=""Inter""`, which is malformed XML, so every `Custom` face broke the document | the row 7 bytes, XML-escaped: `font-family="&quot;Inter&quot;"`. Generic families' bytes are unchanged |
| 10 | `nopal-style-test-deps` | build | — | building `nopal_style`'s tests (`opam install -t`, `dune runtest`) | `alcotest` | also `ocamlfind {with-test}`, for a test that checks a stack with no last resort fails to compile |
| 11 | `nopal-svg-test-deps` | build | — | building `nopal_svg`'s tests | no XML parser | also `xmlm {with-test}`, which parses rendered SVG. No runtime or bundle effect |
| 12 | `kitchen-sink-font-and-links` | example | web | anyone copying the kitchen sink | typography had no stack; both links underlined at the browser's offset on hover | typography gains a `"Geist", system-ui, sans-serif` row and a `"Nopal Missing Face", monospace` row beside a `monospace` reference row; the in-app link's hover underline sits at `3px`, the external link's is unchanged |

What did **not** move, recorded so a reader does not go looking.
`Scene.text ~font_family` still takes one `Font.family`; scene text has no
stack. `Text.font_family`'s signature is unchanged, and a single family still
has no last resort, so a missing face still falls back to the engine's default.
No font is loaded: there is no `@font-face` registration. A `("style", …)` pair
in `~attrs` is still written after the typed inline styles and replaces them,
for a font stack as for every other `Style.t` field.

**Heading answers that moved — read this on a pin bump.**
**Every exhaustive `match` on `Element.t` stops compiling** (row 1): the type
gains a `Heading` arm, placed after `Link`, and the missing arm trips warning 8,
an error under dune's default dev profile. Add the arm; a renderer that walks
the tree visits its one `child`, as it does a `Link`'s. A match ending in a
`_ ->` catch-all compiles unchanged and sends every heading to that branch.
Nothing else stops compiling: every other row is additive, or changes what a
renderer writes or what the kitchen sink renders.

"Before" is the tree at commit `8c39fad`. The Where column names the renderer
whose answer moved: web, the structural `Test_renderer`, or both. Rows 8–14 are
the kitchen sink's rendered tree, which consumers copy: every title that read as
a heading is now one, and each title's own text node is unchanged inside it, so
a selector on the title's `span` or its text still finds it. No test reads this
table. The behaviour each row describes is tested in the `nopal_element`,
`nopal_test`, `nopal_web` and kitchen-sink suites and, for web, by the
kitchen-sink Playwright and axe cases, but an edit to the text alone reddens no
test.

| 12 | `kitchen-sink-responsive-typography-title` | example | web | "Responsive typography" in Responsive Design | `div > span`, the style on the `div` | `h3 > span`, with `title_text_style` moved to the `h3` as its `~style` |
