| 14 | `kitchen-sink-headings-section` | example | web | anyone copying the kitchen sink | no Headings section | a "Headings" section (`data-testid="headings-section"`) right after Typography: an `H2` title, an `H3`–`H6` chain sized from one scale, an unstyled `H3` beside plain text, and an `H3` with a 1.5rem size and a hover underline, so its style goes to a class rule (`examples/kitchen_sink/sub_headings.ml`) |

What did **not** move, recorded so a reader does not go looking.
`Element.text` and `styled_text` still render a `span`, and no existing
element's rendered output changes outside rows 8–14. An unstyled `button` or
`link` still shows the browser's defaults: the reset reaches headings only.
`Style.t` gains no field, and `Style.layout` still has no margin. Nopal still
checks no heading order. `nopal_ui` renders no heading: `Modal`'s title is
still authored by its caller inside `body`, and making it a heading is the
caller's choice. The Typography section's "Heading scale" rows are a type-scale
demonstration and stay styled text, not headings. The `Test_renderer` selectors
are unchanged; `By_tag "h2"` finds a level-2 heading, but `find_heading` is the
documented query.

**Alignment answers that moved — read this on a pin bump.**
`layout.main_align` and `layout.cross_align` no longer share a type: the main
axis keeps `Style.align`, now `Start | Center | End_ | Space_between`, and the
cross axis takes the new `Style.cross_align`, `Start | Center | End_ | Stretch`.
**Every `Stretch` written for the main axis stops compiling** (row 1): the
error says there is no constructor `Stretch` within `Style.align`. **Every
`Space_between` written for the cross axis stops compiling** (row 2): the error
says there is no constructor `Space_between` within `Style.cross_align`. **Every
exhaustive `match` that names a removed value stops compiling** (row 3): an arm
for `Stretch` on a main-axis value, or for `Space_between` on a cross-axis
value. **A binding whose type no longer matches the field it reaches stops
compiling** (row 4). Code that wrote `cross_align = Some Space_between` or
`main_align = Some Stretch` compiled before but never rendered as written: the
browser dropped the first and stretched the children as though nothing had
been set, and laid the second out exactly as `Start`. Each "Now" says what to
write instead, and the replacement keeps what actually rendered.

"Before" is the tree at commit `9870b5b`. The Where column names the output
whose answer moved: web (the CSS the DOM backend writes, inline and in class
rules), or all of them for a compile break. No test reads this table. The
behaviour each row describes is tested in `nopal_style`'s `Style` suite and its
compile-fail cram test, the web `Style_css` suite, the kitchen-sink alignment
suite and the kitchen-sink Playwright cases, but an edit to the text alone
reddens no test.

| # | Key | Visible | Where | When | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `main-align-stretch-removed` | compile | all | a `main_align = Some Stretch` literal, or any `Stretch` of type `Style.align` | compiled; the web backend emitted `justify-content: stretch`, which the browser accepts and lays out exactly as `flex-start` | removed. Replace with `Start` for the same geometry, or with `flex_grow` or a `Fill` size on the children if filling the axis was meant |
| 2 | `cross-align-space-between-removed` | compile | all | a `cross_align = Some Space_between` literal | compiled; the web backend emitted `align-items: space-between`, which the browser drops, so the children stretched | removed. Replace with `Some Stretch` or `None`, which is what rendered. Distributing a wrapping container's lines has no replacement: no field of `Style.layout` expresses it |
| 3 | `align-match-removed-arm` | compile | all | an exhaustive `match` on a `Style.align` naming `Stretch`, or on a `layout.cross_align` naming `Space_between` | compiled | the arm is a compile error. Fix: delete it |
| 4 | `layout-cross-align-retyped` | compile | all | a value annotated `Style.align` passed to `cross_align`, or an unannotated binding (which now resolves to `Style.cross_align`) passed to `main_align` | `cross_align : align option` | `cross_align : cross_align option`. Fix: annotate the binding `: Style.align` or `: Style.cross_align`, or retype it. A kept constructor written straight into either field compiles unchanged |
| 5 | `style-cross-align` | additive | all | `Nopal_style.Style` | — | `type cross_align = Start \| Center \| End_ \| Stretch` `equal_align : align -> align -> bool` and `equal_cross_align : cross_align -> cross_align -> bool`, each of which holds exactly when both are the same constructor. `equal_layout` compares `main_align` and `cross_align` with them |
| 6 | `web-alignment-tokens` | bytes | web | the `justify-content` and `align-items` the DOM backend writes, inline and in interaction rules | `justify-content: stretch` and `align-items: space-between` could be emitted | neither can. Every kept value emits the bytes it emitted before: `justify-content` `flex-start`, `center`, `flex-end`, `space-between`; `align-items` `flex-start`, `center`, `flex-end`, `stretch` |
| 7 | `kitchen-sink-alignment-section` | example | web | anyone copying the kitchen sink | no Alignment section | an "Alignment" section (`data-testid="alignment-section"`) right after Layout: one row per main-axis value (`align-main-start`, `-center`, `-end`, `-space-between`) and one per cross-axis value (`align-cross-start`, `-center`, `-end`, `-stretch`), the cross rows holding boxes of unequal height (`examples/kitchen_sink/sub_alignment.ml`) |

What did **not** move, recorded so a reader does not go looking. A constructor
written straight into a `layout` field compiles unchanged where its value is
kept: `Start`, `Center` and `End_` on either axis, `Space_between` in
`main_align` and `Stretch` in `cross_align`. The field's type picks the
constructor, with no warning, and the emitted bytes are those listed in row 6.
The name `Style.align` still names the main axis, so an existing `: Style.align`
annotation on a main-axis value compiles. Nothing emits `align-content` or
`align-self`, before or now, and no element takes per-child alignment. The
structural `Test_renderer` carries `Style.t` as written and interprets no
alignment, so a structural test reads the value the browser applies.

#### Telemetry harness (`Nopal_test.Telemetry_test`)

Native, browser-free harness that drives a real app through the recording MVU
loop (via `Runtime.create_with_telemetry` + an immediate scheduler) and asserts
on the recorded event history. See the E2E Telemetry section for the layered
model the events come from.

```ocaml
Telemetry_test.run_with_telemetry :
  (module Nopal_mvu.App.S with type model = 'model and type msg = 'msg) ->
  ?serialize_msg:('msg -> string) ->
  ?serialize_model:('model -> string) ->
  'msg list ->
  'model * Nopal_runtime.Telemetry.event list
(* Dispatches each message synchronously through the real loop, recording every
   message/transition/command/subscription, then returns the final model and the
   ordered event list. If application code raises mid-sequence, the recorded
   history is dumped to stderr and the ORIGINAL exception is re-raised unchanged
   (backtrace intact). The log is cleared on exit either way. *)

(* Assertion helpers — each raises Failure with a diagnostic listing the actual
   recorded events. fragment = substring match, the cross-language contract. *)
Telemetry_test.assert_dispatched     : Telemetry.event list -> fragment:string -> unit
  (* some Message contains fragment *)
Telemetry_test.assert_sequence       : Telemetry.event list -> fragments:string list -> unit
  (* each fragment appears as a Message in order; unrelated events allowed between *)
Telemetry_test.assert_model_contains : Telemetry.event list -> fragment:string -> unit
  (* some Model_transition.after contains fragment *)
```

### Web Renderer (`nopal_web`)

Mount an app to the DOM (the only package with browser dependencies):

```ocaml
Nopal_web.mount :
  ?safe_area_source:((Nopal_element.Viewport.safe_area -> unit) -> unit -> unit)
  -> ?on_error:(string -> unit)
  -> ?write_clipboard:
       (string -> ((unit, Nopal_mvu.Clipboard.error) result -> unit) -> unit)
  -> ?open_external:
       (Nopal_element.Url.t
        -> ((unit, Nopal_element.Link.open_error) result -> unit) -> unit)
  -> (module Nopal_mvu.App.S with type model = 'model and type msg = 'msg)
  -> Brr.El.t -> Nopal_web.mounted      (* { unmount : unit -> unit } *)
(* Records no telemetry and installs no bridge.
   ?open_external shows a URL outside the app and resolves with the outcome.
   Given, links render for a Link.Webview host: a primary or middle click on an
   External link is handed to it and the page does not navigate; its first
   Error is dispatched as the link's on_open_failed and later answers are
   absorbed; a raise before any answer is Failed with the exception's
   constructor name, never its message. Omitted, links render for a
   Link.Browser host.
   REFUSAL: on a page that defines __TAURI_INTERNALS__ with ?open_external
   omitted, mount creates no runtime and renders no app. It writes this fault
   into the target and sends the same text to ?on_error, and unmount is inert:
     "nopal_web refused to mount: this page runs in a Tauri webview and the
      mount was given no ~open_external, so a link would navigate the webview
      away from the app. Mount through Nopal_tauri_mount, which supplies one."
   Reading that one global is all nopal_web knows of Tauri; it depends on no
   Tauri package.
   Each mount appends its own <style data-nopal> to <head>, opening with the
   scoped heading reset (see Element DSL -> Headings). A DOM shim that mounts
   under Node must implement the sheet's insertRule. *)

(* Telemetry sibling of mount — see the E2E Telemetry section (Layer 2) *)
Nopal_web.mount_with_telemetry :
  ?safe_area_source:((Nopal_element.Viewport.safe_area -> unit) -> unit -> unit)
  -> ?on_error:(string -> unit)
  -> ?write_clipboard:
       (string -> ((unit, Nopal_mvu.Clipboard.error) result -> unit) -> unit)
  -> ?open_external:
       (Nopal_element.Url.t
        -> ((unit, Nopal_element.Link.open_error) result -> unit) -> unit)
  -> (module Nopal_mvu.App.S with type model = 'model and type msg = 'msg)
  -> ?serialize_msg:('msg -> string)      (* default: fun _ -> "<opaque>" *)
  -> ?serialize_model:('model -> string)  (* default: fun _ -> "<opaque>" *)
  -> Brr.El.t -> Nopal_web.mounted_with_telemetry
(* Builds a recording runtime, drives it, installs window.__nopal_telemetry__
   over its handle, and returns { telemetry : Telemetry.handle; unmount } (the
   handle is the input to Layer 3). Presence is the function name + return
   type, never an optional argument. ?write_clipboard is the handler behind
   Cmd.write_clipboard; see Commands -> Clipboard. ?open_external is as on
   mount, and so is the refusal: a refused mount installs no bridge, and its
   telemetry handle comes from a runtime that is created (so init runs) and
   never started (so it records nothing). *)

(* Browser platform: navigation + storage capabilities *)
module Platform_web : Nopal_platform.Platform.S   (* storage = Nopal_storage_web.Make () *)
```

### Web Storage (`nopal_web`)

Browser localStorage access. All operations are synchronous — safe to call directly from `update`. Values persist across page reloads within the same origin.

```ocaml
Nopal_web.Storage.get    : string -> string option   (* read key from localStorage *)
Nopal_web.Storage.set    : string -> string -> unit   (* write key/value; ignores quota errors *)
Nopal_web.Storage.remove : string -> unit             (* delete key; no-op if absent *)
Nopal_web.Storage.clear  : unit -> unit               (* remove all keys *)
```

### Tauri Bindings (`nopal_tauri`)

Typed OCaml bindings to the Tauri JavaScript API for desktop/mobile targets. Depends on `nopal_mvu` for `Task.t`. All async functions return `Task.t` values — use `Cmd.task` to run them from `update`. If the Tauri runtime is not available, tasks never resolve.

```ocaml
(* App — application metadata from tauri.conf.json *)
val App.get_name          : string Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val App.get_version       : string Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val App.get_tauri_version : string Nopal_mvu.Task.t

(* Os — host platform detection via Tauri os plugin *)
type Os.platform = Windows | MacOS | Linux | IOS | Android
val Os.platform           : Os.platform Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Os.to_string          : Os.platform -> string
val Os.platform_of_string : string -> Os.platform option

(* Window — window management *)
type Window.size = { width : int; height : int }
val Window.set_title      : string -> unit Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Window.set_fullscreen : bool -> unit Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Window.is_fullscreen  : bool Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Window.minimize       : unit Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Window.maximize       : unit Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Window.unmaximize     : unit Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Window.is_maximized   : bool Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Window.close          : unit Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Window.set_size       : Window.size -> unit Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Window.inner_size     : Window.size Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Window.is_visible     : bool Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Window.show           : unit Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Window.hide           : unit Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Window.set_focus      : unit Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Window.center         : unit Nopal_mvu.Task.t

(* Platform — navigation + storage capabilities for Tauri webview *)
module Platform_tauri : Nopal_platform.Platform.S   (* storage = Nopal_storage_tauri.Make () *)

(* Android hardware back button — pick ONE of these two, never both. They are
   independent listeners on the same `nopal:back-pressed` event, so calling both
   makes one press do both things. *)
val Platform_tauri.enable_hardware_back : unit -> unit
  (* ROUTED apps only: turns each press into window.history.back(). That raises a
     popstate — and so reaches Router.on_navigate — only if the app pushed a
     history entry. An app with no router pushes none, so the press does nothing
     at all, and on Android OnBackPressedCallback(true) has already swallowed it,
     so the app does not background either. *)
val Platform_tauri.on_back_pressed : 'msg -> 'msg Nopal_mvu.Sub.t
  (* ROUTER-LESS apps: dispatches msg on each press, no history round trip.
     No setup-time dispatch — a press is an event, not a signal. *)

(* Tray — system tray icon subscriptions + task bindings *)
(* Requires tray-icon:default capability and trayIcon in tauri.conf.json *)
val Tray.on_click       : 'msg -> 'msg Nopal_mvu.Sub.t
val Tray.on_double_click : 'msg -> 'msg Nopal_mvu.Sub.t
val Tray.set_icon       : string -> unit Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Tray.set_tooltip    : string -> unit Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Tray.set_visible    : bool -> unit Nopal_mvu.Task.t

(* Store — persistent key-value storage via tauri-plugin-store *)
(* Requires store:default capability and tauri-plugin-store registered *)
val Store.get    : string -> (string option, string) result Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Store.set    : string -> string -> (unit, string) result Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Store.delete : string -> (unit, string) result Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Store.clear  : unit -> (unit, string) result Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Store.save   : unit -> (unit, string) result Nopal_mvu.Task.t

(* Opener — the Tauri handler behind an External link, via
   tauri-plugin-opener's plugin:opener|open_url. Not called from update:
   Nopal_tauri_mount passes it to Nopal_web.mount ~open_external. Requires the
   plugin registered and "opener:allow-open-url" plus
   "opener:allow-default-urls" granted (see "Links and the Tauri mount" below).
   Resolves exactly once: Ok when the host handed the URL to the system's
   default application; Error Not_permitted on an ACL refusal, an unregistered
   plugin, or a URL outside the plugin's scope; Error (Failed reason) otherwise
   — including "Tauri runtime not available" outside Tauri, and a throwing
   invoke. Every occurrence of the URL in a reason is replaced by "<url>". *)
val Opener.open_url :
  Nopal_element.Url.t -> ((unit, Nopal_element.Link.open_error) result -> unit) -> unit

(* Clipboard — the Tauri handler for Cmd.write_clipboard, via
   tauri-plugin-clipboard-manager. Not called from update: Nopal_tauri_mount
   passes it to Nopal_web.mount ~write_clipboard. Requires the plugin registered and
   "clipboard-manager:allow-write-text" granted (see Commands → Clipboard).
   Resolves exactly once: Ok, Error Not_permitted on an ACL refusal, or
   Error (Failed reason) — including "Tauri runtime not available" outside
   Tauri. *)
val Clipboard.write :
  string -> ((unit, Nopal_mvu.Clipboard.error) result -> unit) -> unit

(* Event — emit returns Task.t; listen uses callbacks (maps to Sub.custom) *)
type Event.event = { payload : string }
type Event.unlisten = unit -> unit
val Event.emit   : string -> string -> unit Nopal_mvu.Task.t
val Event.listen : string -> (Event.event -> unit) -> (Event.unlisten -> unit) -> unit

(* Telemetry — Layer 3 host surface (opt-in). See the E2E Telemetry section. *)
val Telemetry.expose : Nopal_runtime.Telemetry.handle -> unit
  (* Registers a forwarder mirroring each event into the Tauri host process,
     enabling get_telemetry from outside the webview. No-op surface unless called. *)
val Telemetry.get_telemetry :
  unit -> (Nopal_runtime.Telemetry.event list, string) result Nopal_mvu.Task.t
  (* Queries the host-side mirror via Ipc.invoke. Async (Task.t), not a sync
     result — the IPC reply arrives via a promise (RFC 0110 Decision 3). *)
```

Usage pattern — `Cmd.task` + `Task.Syntax` composition:

```ocaml
open Nopal_mvu.Task.Syntax

(* Single task *)
| GetAppName ->
    let task = let+ name = Nopal_tauri.App.get_name in GotName name in
    (model, Cmd.task task)

(* Chained tasks *)
| ToggleFullscreen ->
    let task =
      let* fs = Nopal_tauri.Window.is_fullscreen in
      let+ () = Nopal_tauri.Window.set_fullscreen (not fs) in
      FullscreenToggled
    in
    (model, Cmd.task task)

(* Platform_tauri — routing in Tauri apps *)
let router =
  Router.create
    ~platform:(module Nopal_tauri.Platform_tauri)
    ~parse ~to_path ~not_found:Home

(* Event.listen maps to Sub.custom (not Task.t) *)
let subscriptions _model =
  Sub.custom "tauri-event" (fun dispatch ->
    Nopal_tauri.Event.listen "my-event"
      (fun ev -> dispatch (GotEvent ev.payload))
      (fun _unlisten -> ());
    fun () -> () (* cleanup *))

(* Tray — hide window to tray, restore on click *)
let subscriptions model =
  let base = My_app.subscriptions model in
  Sub.batch [ base; Nopal_tauri.Tray.on_click TrayClicked ]

| HideToTray ->
    let cmd = Cmd.task (let+ () = Nopal_tauri.Window.hide in TrayRestored) in
    (model, cmd)
| TrayClicked ->
    let cmd = Cmd.task
      (let* () = Nopal_tauri.Window.show in
       let+ () = Nopal_tauri.Window.set_focus in
       TrayRestored)
    in
    (model, cmd)

(* Store — set + save + get pattern (requires: open Nopal_mvu.Task.Syntax) *)
| SaveTheme ->
    let task =
      let* set_result = Nopal_tauri.Store.set "theme" "dark" in
      match set_result with
      | Error msg -> Task.return (SaveFailed msg)
      | Ok () ->
          let+ save_result = Nopal_tauri.Store.save () in
          match save_result with
          | Ok ()     -> ThemeSaved
          | Error msg -> SaveFailed msg
    in
    (model, Cmd.task task)

| LoadTheme ->
    let task = let+ r = Nopal_tauri.Store.get "theme" in GotTheme r in
    (model, Cmd.task task)
```

#### Links and the Tauri mount (`nopal_tauri.mount`)

Mount a Tauri app through `Nopal_tauri_mount`, never through `Nopal_web.mount`
directly. It is the sub-library `nopal_tauri.mount` (add `nopal_tauri.mount` to
the executable's dune `libraries`); `nopal_tauri` itself stays free of UI
packages. It renders with `Nopal_web` and supplies every host handler a webview
needs, so a Tauri app cannot get browser link behaviour by forgetting an
argument:

```ocaml
Nopal_tauri_mount.mount :
  ?safe_area_source:((Nopal_element.Viewport.safe_area -> unit) -> unit -> unit)
  -> ?on_error:(string -> unit)
  -> (module Nopal_mvu.App.S with type model = 'model and type msg = 'msg)
  -> Brr.El.t -> Nopal_web.mounted
(* Nopal_web.mount with ~write_clipboard:Nopal_tauri.Clipboard.write and
   ~open_external:Nopal_tauri.Opener.open_url. ?safe_area_source and ?on_error
   pass through unchanged, so supplying Platform_tauri.safe_area_source on a
   given platform stays the caller's choice. *)

Nopal_tauri_mount.mount_with_telemetry :
  ?safe_area_source:((Nopal_element.Viewport.safe_area -> unit) -> unit -> unit)
  -> ?on_error:(string -> unit)
  -> (module Nopal_mvu.App.S with type model = 'model and type msg = 'msg)
  -> ?serialize_msg:('msg -> string) -> ?serialize_model:('model -> string)
  -> Brr.El.t -> Nopal_web.mounted_with_telemetry
(* Nopal_web.mount_with_telemetry with the same two handlers. *)
```

With it, links render for a webview (`Link.Webview`; the table under Element
DSL → Links): a primary or middle click on an `External` link, modified or not,
opens the URL in the system browser and the webview stays on the app; a
`Route` link treats a modified or middle click as a plain click. A failed open
dispatches the link's `on_open_failed` with `Not_permitted` or `Failed reason`.
`Nopal_web.mount` on a Tauri page without `~open_external` refuses to mount
and shows why in the window.

The Tauri host needs three edits:

```toml
# src-tauri/Cargo.toml, under [dependencies]
tauri-plugin-opener = "2"
```

```rust
// src-tauri/src/lib.rs, on the tauri::Builder chain
.plugin(tauri_plugin_opener::init())
```

```json
// src-tauri/capabilities/default.json, in the "permissions" list
"opener:allow-open-url",
"opener:allow-default-urls",
```

Grant those two lines and nothing else. `opener:allow-open-url` lets the
webview call `open_url` and carries no scope; `opener:allow-default-urls`
grants no command and scopes `open_url` to `mailto:*`, `tel:*`, `http://*` and
`https://*` — exactly the schemes a `Url.t` can carry (observed in the
generated `src-tauri/gen/schemas/acl-manifests.json` for `tauri-plugin-opener`
2.5.3, the version this repository's `Cargo.lock` holds). Without the scope
line every open is refused, and the link dispatches `Not_permitted`.
`opener:default` is not a shortcut: it also grants `allow-reveal-item-in-dir`,
which lets the webview reveal any file in the system's file manager. Audit
what a capability grants from that generated manifest, not from this list:
a `:default` entry expands to permissions the list never names.

**Recheck on a `tauri` or `tauri-plugin-opener` version bump.**
`Nopal_tauri.Opener` recognises a refusal by the exact words of the versions
named in `backends/nopal_tauri/opener.ml`: tauri 2.10.3's ACL refusals (the
release build's `Command plugin:opener|open_url not allowed by ACL`, the debug
build's messages beginning `opener.open_url not allowed` or
`opener.open_url explicitly denied`, and `plugin opener not found`) and the
plugin's scope refusal, which begins `Not allowed to open url ` followed by the
URL. When either locked version changes, re-read those sources and update the
decoder if a message is reworded. Until then a reworded refusal arrives as
`Error (Failed <the host's message, URL redacted>)` instead of
`Not_permitted` — still exactly once.

## E2E Telemetry

Nopal's cross-platform E2E correctness contract is the MVU telemetry log, not
DOM assertions (ADR 0108): tests trigger interactions with standard automation,
then assert that the right messages were dispatched and the model reached the
right state. Telemetry is a **layered, explicit, type-tracked capability** — never
build-gated, never default-on. Each more-exposed surface is a strictly more
explicit opt-in built from the layer below.

| Layer | Entry point | Grants | Exposure |
|-------|-------------|--------|----------|
| 0 | `Runtime.create` | A runtime that records nothing | none |
| 1 | `Runtime.create_with_telemetry` | In-process recording + a `Telemetry.handle` (the only way to get one) | in-process |
| 2 | `Nopal_web.mount_with_telemetry` (returns the handle) | `window.__nopal_telemetry__` browser bridge | browser/JS |
| 3 | `Nopal_tauri.Telemetry.expose handle` | `get_telemetry` query + `simulate_*` synthetic IPC | Tauri host |

A `Telemetry.handle` is **unforgeable**: the public `Telemetry` signature exposes
`type handle` abstractly with query operations but no constructor, so the only way
to obtain one is `create_with_telemetry` (or a mount that calls it). On/off is
carried by *which constructor / which mount* you call — never an optional argument.
Each higher layer consumes a handle, so you cannot install the browser bridge or
the IPC surface without having explicitly mounted a telemetry-bearing runtime.
Presence is therefore always greppable and deliberate.

**Application-gating responsibility.** The framework guarantees telemetry is never
*implicit* — every surface is explicit, type-tracked, and auditable. It does NOT
strip telemetry from release builds (that would forbid legitimate release-build QA
and release-only-defect diagnosis). The browser bridge and the Tauri synthetic/
query commands expose application state and synthetic triggers, so **the application
is responsible for gating their reachability** in release builds (e.g. behind
authentication, a QA-only config flag, or remote config). The framework makes the
choice explicit and greppable; it does not make it safe-by-fiat.

```ocaml
(* The application owns the policy; the framework provides composable capability.
   A Tauri app mounts through Nopal_tauri_mount: Nopal_web.mount* refuses to
   mount on a Tauri page without ~open_external. *)
match Config.telemetry_mode config with   (* the app's enum, the app's config *)
| Off ->
    ignore (Nopal_tauri_mount.mount (module App) target)
| Record_and_expose ->
    let mounted =
      Nopal_tauri_mount.mount_with_telemetry (module App)
        ~serialize_msg ~serialize_model target
    in
    Nopal_tauri.Telemetry.expose mounted.Nopal_web.telemetry   (* Layer 3, optional, from the same handle *)
```

### Telemetry event log (`Nopal_runtime.Telemetry`)

The public re-export is the narrowed query view — `event`, abstract `handle`, and
queries only. `recorder`, `create`, and the recording ops are hidden so a handle is
unforgeable outside `Runtime`.

```ocaml
type Telemetry.event =
  | Message of string                                    (* dispatched msg, serialised or "<opaque>" *)
  | Model_transition of { before : string; after : string }  (* one update's state change *)
  | Command of string                                    (* command issued, by Cmd.describe label *)
  | Subscription of string                               (* subscription fired, by Sub.describe label *)

type Telemetry.handle   (* abstract, no constructor *)
val Telemetry.events    : handle -> event list           (* recorded events, oldest first *)
val Telemetry.clear     : handle -> unit
val Telemetry.on_record : handle -> (event -> unit) -> unit -> unit  (* sink per event; returns a disposer that unregisters it; sinks compose *)
val Telemetry.pp_events : Format.formatter -> event list -> unit  (* failure diagnostics *)
```

Runtime constructors (`Nopal_runtime.Runtime.Make(A)`):

```ocaml
val create :
  ?focus:(string -> unit) ->
  ?scroll_by:(string -> Nopal_element.Scroll_delta.t -> unit) ->
  ?write_clipboard:
    (string -> ((unit, Nopal_mvu.Clipboard.error) result -> unit) -> unit) ->
  ?schedule_after:(int -> (unit -> unit) -> unit) ->
  unit -> t
(* Records nothing. Behaviour unchanged from the pre-telemetry runtime.
   [scroll_by] is the platform callback implementing Cmd.scroll_by; like
   [focus] it defaults to a no-op, so a backend that renders no elements leaves
   the request inert rather than reporting it. The web backend passes a callback
   that queues the request for the drain running after the frame's DOM patch.
   [write_clipboard text resolve] implements Cmd.write_clipboard and calls
   [resolve]; the runtime delivers the first call and absorbs later calls and a
   raise. Unlike [focus] it is not a no-op by default: the
   default resolves [Error Unavailable] at once, because the application is
   waiting for the outcome message. *)

val create_with_telemetry :
  ?focus:(string -> unit) ->
  ?scroll_by:(string -> Nopal_element.Scroll_delta.t -> unit) ->
  ?write_clipboard:
    (string -> ((unit, Nopal_mvu.Clipboard.error) result -> unit) -> unit) ->
  ?schedule_after:(int -> (unit -> unit) -> unit) ->
  ?serialize_msg:(A.msg -> string) ->        (* default: fun _ -> "<opaque>" *)
  ?serialize_model:(A.model -> string) ->    (* default: fun _ -> "<opaque>" *)
  unit -> t * Telemetry.handle
(* Records every dispatched message, model transition, command, and subscription
   firing; returns the only handle in existence for this runtime. A plain `create`
   runtime does zero per-message recording work (REQ-N1, by inspection). *)
```

Constructor labels for the `Command`/`Subscription` events (stable strings the
fragment assertions depend on):

```ocaml
val Cmd.describe : 'msg Cmd.t -> string   (* "none" | "batch" | "perform" | "task" | "after" | "focus" | "scroll_by" | "write_clipboard" — never the copied text *)
val Sub.describe : 'msg Sub.t -> string   (* "none" | "batch" | "every" | "on_keydown" | ... | "custom" *)
```

### Browser bridge — `window.__nopal_telemetry__` (Layer 2)

Installed only by `mount_with_telemetry`; absent on a plain `mount`.

```ts
interface NopalTelemetryBridge {
  getEvents(): TelemetryEvent[];                              // full list, then clears
  waitForMessage(fragment: string, timeoutMs: number): Promise<void>;
                                                              // resolves on first matching Message; rejects on timeout
}
```

### Playwright class — `NopalTelemetry` (`test/e2e/tests/nopal-telemetry.ts`)

```ts
class NopalTelemetry {
  constructor(page: Page);                  // wraps window.__nopal_telemetry__ (Layer 2, web only)
  events(): Promise<TelemetryEvent[]>;
  waitForMessage(fragment: string, timeoutMs: number): Promise<void>;
  assertDispatched(fragment: string): Promise<void>;
  assertSequence(fragments: string[]): Promise<void>;
  assertModelContains(fragment: string): Promise<void>;
  attachHistory(testInfo: TestInfo): Promise<void>;   // attach event history to the report before cleanup
}
```

The `NopalTelemetry` class is **web-only**: it wraps the Layer 2 browser bridge.
Layer 3 (Tauri host) is queried from OCaml via `Nopal_tauri.Telemetry.get_telemetry`
or, from a host-side driver, the raw `invoke("get_telemetry")` command. There is no
CI Tauri runtime today (per RFC 0077/0107), so Layer 3 is validated by the manual
checklist in `docs/guides/telemetry-tauri.md`. A headless Tauri E2E harness (which
would let the same assertion spec run against web and Tauri) is tracked in
`ROADMAP.md`.

## Coding Rules

- Never `raise` for recoverable errors — return `('a, error) result`
- Never use catch-all `_` in match where the compiler can enforce exhaustiveness
- No `if/else` chains where `match` on a variant is correct
- No `mutable` fields without a justifying comment
- No inline helpers — helper functions live in dedicated modules with `.mli` files and tests
- No CSS strings in view code — all styling uses `nopal_style` types
- No business logic in `nopal_runtime` or `nopal_web` — they interpret and render only
- `App.update` never produces side effects directly — return `Cmd.t` instead
- Write tests first (TDD) — no `.ml` implementation without a failing test first
- Three test layers required: unit (Alcotest), structural (nopal_test), E2E (Playwright)
- Every PR touching runtime or web must benchmark against `bench/baseline.json` (no >20% regression)

## Project Structure

```
lib/
  nopal_mvu/         — Cmd, Sub, App, Task, Key_chord, Clipboard — depends on nopal_element
                       for the types they carry; zero platform deps
  nopal_element/     — Element.t DSL + Virtual_list + Reveal + Scroll_delta + Submit_route — zero platform deps
  nopal_style/       — Style.t, Text.t, Interaction.t, Cursor.t, Font, Color
                       (Color is the CSS-authoring colour type; distinct from
                       nopal_scene/'s float-RGBA Color)
  nopal_storage/     — Nopal_storage.S, In_memory, With_codec (async key-value contract)
  nopal_platform/    — Router.t, Platform.NAV, Platform.S (storage capability) [renamed from nopal_router]
  nopal_scene/       — Pure scene types: Color, Paint, Transform, Path, Scene
  nopal_draw/        — Scale, Arc (shared arc sweep resolver) + higher-level Path algorithms (re-exports nopal_scene)
  nopal_charts/      — Bar, Line, Area, Pie, Scatter, Sparkline, Heat_map,
                       Trading.Candlestick, Trading.Drawdown, Chart_pane,
                       Color_scale, Domain_window, Viewport, Downsample, Snap
  nopal_http/        — Pure HTTP types + backend abstraction
  nopal_image/       — Buffer, Luma, Sharpness, Config, Processing + Preview + Retention seams (pure pixel data; depends on nopal_mvu, no platform deps)
  nopal_ui/          — High-level UI components (Button, Checkbox, Data_table, Modal, Navigation_bar, Radio_group, Select_input, Slug, Text_input, Toast)
  nopal_runtime/     — Lwd integration + MVU loop; Telemetry (E2E event log)
  nopal_test/        — Pure OCaml test renderer + Telemetry_test harness
backends/
  nopal_web/         — js_of_ocaml + Brr DOM renderer
  nopal_http_web/    — Browser Fetch API backend for nopal_http
  nopal_blob_web/    — Session-local handle ⇄ Brr.Blob.t registry + object URLs (leaf; no renderer dep)
  nopal_image_web/   — Browser canvas pipeline implementing Nopal_image.Processing,
                       plus the object-URL backend for Nopal_image.Preview and
                       the entry-release backend for Nopal_image.Retention.
                       Public module is the seams only; Canvas_ffi, Dimensions and
                       Once sit in the nopal_image_web.internal sub-library
  nopal_storage_web/   — IndexedDB backend implementing Nopal_storage.S
  nopal_storage_tauri/ — Filesystem (tauri-plugin-fs) backend implementing Nopal_storage.S
  nopal_tauri/       — Tauri desktop/mobile bindings (depends on nopal_mvu, nopal_platform)
    mount/           — nopal_tauri.mount sub-library: Nopal_tauri_mount, the Tauri mount
                       entry point (depends on nopal_web)
  nopal_telemetry_wire/ — Shared telemetry event ⇄ JS wire codec (nopal_web + nopal_tauri)
examples/
  counter/           — Hello world
  todomvc/           — Complex app with routing & localStorage
  kitchen_sink/      — Living visual reference for all features. Sections that
                       demonstrate a whole capability rather than one element:
                       "File Input" (pick → multipart upload of the untouched
                       bytes) and, beside it, "Receipt Capture" (pick → canvas
                       decode/downscale/re-encode via nopal_image_web → sharpness
                       verdict and comparison against the previous photo →
                       labelled before/after preview pair of the picked and the
                       as-uploaded photograph, each half naming its own byte
                       length and the as-uploaded half its share of the original
                       → multipart upload of the PROCESSED handle); and "Reveal
                       a child in a scroll container" (arrow-key selection over
                       rows of deliberately unequal height inside a fixed-height
                       scroll container — the container follows because the view
                       names the selected row as its reveal target, with an
                       alignment selector, a row whose key carries a quote and a
                       backslash, and a checkbox gating the arrow keys, which
                       prevent the browser default page-wide and so must not be
                       live all the time); and "Relative scroll of a scroll
                       container" (a fixed-height pane of paragraphs of unequal
                       height that the model moves by half the pane's own
                       visible height — Ctrl+D / Ctrl+U behind their own gating
                       checkbox, since Ctrl+D is the browser's bookmark
                       shortcut and the chords prevent the default; the pane
                       carries a DOM id of its own, which is how a request
                       names it, and it carries a reveal at the same time, so
                       the waypoint control changes the reveal and issues a
                       relative movement in one update; a third control moves
                       the pane a whole viewport and focuses a field further
                       down it in the same update, which is where the last
                       stage becomes visible — focus is applied after the
                       relative movement and takes no preventScroll, so the
                       browser's own scroll-into-view decides where the pane
                       rests; and the section is the visible form of the
                       order all three writers are applied in); and
                       "Focus-revealed note" (a focusable container that shows a
                       note while focus is anywhere inside it and hides it once
                       focus has left the whole container — the
                       keyboard-accessible tooltip, where the model and not a
                       style rule decides what is on screen. The note carries a
                       control of its own, so tabbing from the container into
                       the note is on screen as the case that must fire no edge
                       at all; a reset control sits immediately before the
                       container in tab order, giving a keyboard-driven test a
                       fixed place to start from instead of counting tab stops
                       from the top of the page; and the reveal has exactly one
                       writer — the two focus edges — so the reset deliberately
                       leaves it alone); and "A Fixed size must not shrink" (a
                       box declaring a fixed width and a fixed height beside a
                       Fill sibling whose text carries a token with no break
                       opportunity in it, plus a row of three fixed columns
                       declared wider than the row holding them — one control
                       stops the sibling's line breaking, which is what makes it
                       demand more room than the pair has, and another flips the
                       pair's own axis, which moves the fixed box's main axis
                       from its width to its height with no change to that box's
                       own style. Nothing here is assertable from the element
                       tree: whether a declared size survived is a measurement of
                       rendered geometry, so the structural suite pins only the
                       controls and the fixtures and the claim itself is measured
                       in a browser); and, beside it, "A floor of zero lets a
                       scrolling descendant scroll" (a bounded column of a
                       settled height holding a trailing band and, through an
                       intermediate column, a scroll pane whose content
                       overflows — one control declares min_height = Some 0. on
                       that intermediate column. Without it the column cannot be
                       reduced below its own content, so the pane never scrolls
                       and the band is laid out past the bounded column's bottom
                       edge; with it the column gives way, the overflow goes back
                       to the pane and the band comes home. The floor is on the
                       intermediate column and neither of its neighbours because
                       a floor on either is inert — a scroll container's own
                       automatic minimum is already zero, and a declared height
                       already caps one — which is why the fixture has three
                       levels. Nothing here is assertable from the element tree
                       either; the structural suite pins that the control reaches
                       that column and no other and that the fixture is still
                       overconstrained, and the geometry is measured in a
                       browser). Each lives in
                       its own sub_*.ml/.mli with its own structural suite;
                       the receipt one is
                       examples/kitchen_sink/sub_receipt_flow.ml, the reveal one
                       examples/kitchen_sink/sub_reveal_list.ml, the
                       relative-scroll one
                       examples/kitchen_sink/sub_scroll_pane.ml, the
                       focus one examples/kitchen_sink/sub_focus_reveal.ml and
                       the fixed-size one
                       examples/kitchen_sink/sub_fixed_size.ml and the
                       minimum-size one examples/kitchen_sink/sub_min_size.ml
  dashboard/         — Charts showcase
test/
  unit/              — Alcotest tests per package
  e2e/               — Playwright + TypeScript
bench/               — js-framework-benchmark + baseline.json
```

## Build Commands

```bash
just                   # build + test + fmt + lint (run before every commit)
just build             # opam exec -- dune build
just build-native      # verify DSL packages compile without js_of_ocaml
just test              # opam exec -- dune runtest
just serve-counter     # build + serve counter example
just serve-todomvc     # build + serve todomvc example
just serve-kitchen     # build + serve kitchen sink example
just serve-dashboard   # build + serve dashboard example
just bench             # run benchmark suite
just bench-compare     # compare against bench/baseline.json
```
